title: Recurrence of the planar horizontal-new vertical-old walk
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Start at the origin in Z^2; after first visiting a site step horizontally with either sign equally likely, and after a repeat visit step vertically with either sign equally likely. Does any site receive infinitely many visits with positive probability?
statement_caveat: The source indexing omits the first step; use its intended new-site rule also at time zero. The analogous four- and three-dimensional results do not decide this planar model.
source: Probability on Trees and Networks, paperback electronic version 19 August 2026
why_important: A clean planar test case for self-interacting walks, where martingale and Markov tools both fail.
where_it_stands: The three- and four-dimensional analogues are settled; the rule is explicit and two-dimensional.

title: Percolation threshold on arbitrary geodesic Cayley spanning trees
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: If T is any geodesic spanning tree rooted at the identity of a Cayley graph of growth rate b, must br(T)=b, equivalently must its Bernoulli bond percolation threshold be 1/b?
statement_caveat: The branching-number/percolation equivalence is a theorem of the source. The question is stated there geometrically; its probability formulation is recorded transparently. Lexicographically minimal spanning trees satisfy it.
source: Probability on Trees and Networks, paperback electronic version 19 August 2026
why_important: Ties the growth of a group to the percolation threshold of its geodesic trees.
where_it_stands: True for free groups and trees; a branching-number comparison for one tree at a time.

title: Singularity of distinct free and wired forest measures
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: If the wired and free uniform spanning-forest measures differ on an infinite network, must they be mutually singular?
statement_caveat: Known for trees and networks with an infinite automorphism orbit. Distinct probability measures need not be singular in general.
source: Probability on Trees and Networks, paperback electronic version 19 August 2026
why_important: A structural dichotomy for the two uniform spanning forest measures.
where_it_stands: Tail triviality and indistinguishability arguments for spanning forests apply directly.

title: Connectivity of minimal forests on graphs roughly isometric to trees
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: If a connected locally finite graph is roughly isometric to a tree, must its free minimal spanning forest be connected almost surely?
statement_caveat: This concerns minimal forests, not uniform forests; Pete-Timar's uniform-forest counterexample cannot be substituted.
source: Probability on Trees and Networks, paperback electronic version 19 August 2026
why_important: Connectivity of the free minimal spanning forest beyond trees.
where_it_stands: Known on trees; rough isometry gives a concrete transfer route.

title: Monotonicity of harmonic dimension under inward bias
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For a nondegenerate supercritical Galton-Watson tree without leaves and 0<=lambda<m, does harmonic-measure dimension of RW_lambda increase with lambda, and is the increase strict?
statement_caveat: On a deterministic regular tree the dimension is constant, so retain the chapter's nondegeneracy assumptions for strictness. Both monotonic and strict clauses are grouped.
source: Probability on Trees and Networks, paperback electronic version 19 August 2026
why_important: Monotonicity of harmonic-measure dimension for biased walk on Galton-Watson trees.
where_it_stands: Explicit dimension formulas through the invariant measure on the space of trees exist.

title: Fluctuations and large deviations of intermediate level sets of the 2D DGFF
domain_name: Gaussian fields, LQG and planar maps
statement: Describe the rate of convergence in Corollary 2.9 (size of the intermediate level set), identify the limit law of the fluctuations of the level set around its limit, and study deviations whose probability tends to zero as N -> infinity.
source: Biskup: Extrema of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field, PIMS-CRM lecture notes
why_important: Second-order behaviour of intermediate level sets of the planar discrete Gaussian free field.
where_it_stands: The first-order limit is proved in the source; the fluctuation question is the next step of that program.

title: Existence of the limit of e^{-alpha h} E nu(f_h) for the DGFF cluster law
domain_name: Gaussian fields, LQG and planar maps
statement: For the cluster law nu and the functionals f_h counting points at depth h in the cluster, the limit lim_{h -> infinity} e^{-alpha h} E_nu(f_h) exists in (0,infinity).
source: Biskup: Extrema of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field, PIMS-CRM lecture notes
why_important: Exact growth of the cluster law that describes local extremes of the DGFF.
where_it_stands: A renewal-type statement about an explicit cluster law already constructed in the source.

title: Subdiffusive upper bound for the Liouville random walk on the DGFF
domain_name: Gaussian fields, LQG and planar maps
statement: For the random walk X on Z^2 driven by the DGFF with parameter beta > 0 (13.9), show that for each delta > 0, P^0_h(|X_T| <= T^{1/psi(beta)} e^{(log T)^{1/2+delta}}) -> 1 in P-probability.
source: Biskup: Extrema of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field, PIMS-CRM lecture notes
why_important: Subdiffusive scaling of the random walk driven by a log-correlated field.
where_it_stands: Upper bounds of the right type are in the source; the problem asks for the matching sharpening.

title: Asymptotic expansion of the critical value of the Hamming graph
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Show that the critical value of percolation on the Hamming graph K_n^d satisfies p_c(K_n^d; lambda) = sum_{i=1}^{d/3} a_i(d) n^{-i} + O(n^{-1-d/3}), with a_1(d) = 1/d; the second-order term was identified by Federico, van der Hofstad, den Hollander and Hulshof.
source: Heydenreich and van der Hofstad: Progress in high-dimensional percolation and random graphs, author version with open problems
why_important: Asymptotic expansion of the critical point of percolation on Hamming graphs.
where_it_stands: Lace-expansion machinery for high-dimensional graphs is developed and the first coefficient is known.

title: Concentration and uniqueness of the giant component above the scaling window on high-dimensional tori
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: For the torus T_{n,d}, d > 6, and p = p_c(1 + eps) with eps -> 0 but eps >> V^{-1/3}, prove that |C_max|/(eps V) -> c in probability and |C_(2)|/(eps V) -> 0, with c the right-derivative of theta at p_c(Z^d).
source: Heydenreich and van der Hofstad: Progress in high-dimensional percolation and random graphs, author version with open problems
why_important: Law of large numbers for the giant component of high-dimensional torus percolation just above criticality.
where_it_stands: The hypercube analogue is proved; the torus requires the same expansion with finite-size control.

title: Critical behaviour of scale-free percolation
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: For scale-free percolation with parameters alpha (long-range exponent) and tau (weight tail), determine when lambda -> theta(lambda) is continuous, identify the critical exponents, and determine the upper critical dimension as a function of alpha and tau.
source: Heydenreich and van der Hofstad: Progress in high-dimensional percolation and random graphs, author version with open problems
why_important: Phase transition of scale-free percolation, a standard spatial model of real networks.
where_it_stands: Continuity and exponent questions with existing long-range lace-expansion and renormalisation tools.

title: Strict FPP comparison in higher dimensions at a large minimum atom
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Extend strict comparison of axial time constants for strictly ordered passage-time laws in increasing-concave order to d>2 when the minimum support value r>0 has mass at least the oriented-percolation threshold.
statement_caveat: More variable means integral phi dF <= integral phi dG for every increasing concave phi. The claim is axial; equality inside an oriented percolation cone cannot be ignored in statements about arbitrary directions.
source: Auffinger, Damron and Hanson: 50 years of first-passage percolation
locator: Question3, PDF p.13; Definition2.8 and Theorem2.12, pp.12-13
why_important: How the first-passage time constant depends on the edge law.
where_it_stands: The planar case is settled; the higher-dimensional comparison asks for an extension of that argument.

title: Critical Bernoulli FPP growth in three dimensions
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: For iid edge times0 with probability p_c(Z^3) and1 otherwise, determine whether E T(0,boundary B(n)) is comparable to log n.
statement_caveat: The target is undirected edge FPP at the three-dimensional bond threshold; planar critical exponents cannot be transferred.
source: Auffinger, Damron and Hanson: 50 years of first-passage percolation
why_important: Critical first-passage percolation in three dimensions.
where_it_stands: The planar answer is known; the question is a single growth rate.

title: Sharp width threshold for the thin-cylinder FPP CLT
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Determine the largest power alpha for which standardized passage times constrained to Z times[-n^alpha,n^alpha]^(d-1) converge to a standard normal law.
statement_caveat: The source defines gamma_F(d) by this threshold under a finite2+delta edge-time moment. A sufficient exponent from the source theorem is not an optimality result.
source: Auffinger, Damron and Hanson: 50 years of first-passage percolation
why_important: Crossover from Gaussian to non-Gaussian behaviour of passage times in thin cylinders.
where_it_stands: A Gaussian limit is known for small widths; the problem is to push the exponent.

title: Geodesic selection by reinforced ants
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: On a finite graph with nest N and food F, ants take edge-weighted random walks until hitting F. Reinforce either a uniformly chosen shortest N-F path in the visited trace, or the loop erasure of the reversed walk. Are all edges whose weights grow linearly contained in shortest N-F paths of the original graph?
statement_caveat: The two reinforcement algorithms form one conjecture family here. The source proves series-parallel and losange cases, not all graphs.
source: Aletti et al.: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models; March2023 workshop, published2025
why_important: Reinforcement dynamics as a model of path selection by learning agents.
where_it_stands: Finite graphs and stochastic-approximation methods; the source proves special graphs.

title: Deterministic limits for trace-reinforced ants
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: When each ant reinforces every edge it visited at least once, do all edge weights divided by the number of ants converge almost surely to deterministic constants on general finite graphs, and does an appropriate edgewise statement hold on Z^2?
statement_caveat: The finite and Z^2 versions are grouped. The underlying paper excludes multiple edges incident to food; the brief workshop statement omits this load-bearing restriction. Its wording main conjecture is interpreted using the immediately preceding trace-process paragraph.
source: Aletti et al.: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models; March2023 workshop, published2025
locator: OpenProblems1-2, PDF p.2; underlying Kious-Mailler-Schapira Conjecture1.1
why_important: Almost sure limits of reinforced edge weights on general finite graphs.
where_it_stands: Stochastic approximation on a finite system; series-parallel cases are worked out.

title: Critical WARM on the integer line
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For WARM on Z with alpha=1 and all vertex firing rates1, prove that each edge count divided by time converges almost surely to1.
statement_caveat: Keep the stochastic count process distinct from its deterministic equilibrium equation.
source: Aletti et al.: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models; March2023 workshop, published2025
why_important: Law of large numbers for a reinforced network model on the integers.
where_it_stands: Explicit conjecture with all parameters fixed; finite-graph cases are known.

title: Local limits for nonaffine attachment with multiple edges
domain_name: Random graphs and networks
statement: Determine local weak limits of preferential-attachment graphs with fixed outgoing degree m>=2 and nonaffine attachment function f, extending the known tree and affine cases.
statement_caveat: State a nonexplosive/noncondensed class of f before expecting a locally finite limit; the source asks for a theory beyond the affine case, not one arbitrary universal formula.
source: Aletti et al.: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models; March2023 workshop, published2025
why_important: Local weak limits of preferential attachment with nonlinear attachment.
where_it_stands: Tree and affine cases are known; the exploration construction extends.

title: Exponential incompressibility of the infinite-volume wired ARW state
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: For every zeta>zeta_s, prove a volume-exponential upper tail for the number of sleepers in an L-sided cube under pi.
statement_caveat: Conditional on existence of pi and the intended mean density. Pairwise negative covariance is not assumed to imply negative association.
source: Levine and Silvestri: Universality conjectures for activated random walk
why_important: Large deviations for activated random walk above the threshold density.
where_it_stands: A volume-exponential tail estimate; the corresponding lower-density bounds are proved.

title: First-order distance constants in finite-variance preferential attachment
domain_name: Random graphs and networks
statement: For affine preferential attachment with m>=2 and delta>0, prove convergence of typical graph distance/log n and diameter/log n to explicit positive constants a<b.
statement_caveat: Two-sided logarithmic bounds are weaker than convergence to constants. The positive-delta regime is the finite-variance degree regime; logarithmic-logarithmic formulas from negative delta do not apply.
source: Van der Hofstad: Stochastic processes on random graphs, Saint-Flour2017
why_important: Exact distance and diameter constants for preferential attachment graphs.
where_it_stands: Upper and lower bounds of the right order exist; the problem is to identify the constants.

title: Second-order extremal hopcount in exponential complete-graph FPP
domain_name: Random graphs and networks
statement: Determine fluctuations of the longest minimum-weight path, both from a fixed root and over all vertex pairs, beyond the first-order e log n and alpha_star log n scales.
statement_caveat: The rooted shortest-path tree is a random recursive tree, for which substantial height refinements already exist. The all-pairs fluctuation target is retained; known rooted results are not new solutions.
source: Van der Hofstad: Stochastic processes on random graphs, Saint-Flour2017
why_important: Fluctuations of extremal weighted paths in random graphs.
where_it_stands: First-order asymptotics are known; second order through exploration processes.

title: Critical window for fixed-outdegree preferential attachment
domain_name: Random graphs and networks
statement: For affine preferential attachment with a fixed m>=2 edges per arriving vertex and delta>0, identify the percolation scaling window and largest critical component sizes.
statement_caveat: The percolation threshold itself is covered by later work2312.14085. The2025 growing-graph window theorem concerns models with independently attached edges; it is not automatically the fixed-outdegree model asked here.
source: Van der Hofstad: Stochastic processes on random graphs, Saint-Flour2017
why_important: The critical window of percolation on preferential attachment graphs.
where_it_stands: Windows for Erdos-Renyi and configuration models give the template.

title: Two competing largest-component scales in barely subcritical configuration models
domain_name: Random graphs and networks
statement: Under convergence of third degree moments, prove that the largest barely subcritical configuration-model component has order max{d_max/epsilon_n, epsilon_n^(-2)log(n epsilon_n^3)} in the regime specified by the source.
statement_caveat: The asymptotic regime must have epsilon_n tending to0 with n epsilon_n^3 large; otherwise the displayed logarithm is not the intended barely-subcritical scale. Infinite-third-moment results are a different regime.
source: Van der Hofstad: Stochastic processes on random graphs, Saint-Flour2017
why_important: Largest component of a barely subcritical configuration model under minimal moment assumptions.
where_it_stands: A precise order to prove, with matching known results under stronger hypotheses.

title: Largest growing fork-join batch compatible with asymptotic independence
domain_name: Queueing and stochastic networks
statement: Determine how quickly the number k(n) of tasks per uniformly routed job can grow while the corresponding k(n) stationary queues remain asymptotically independent.
statement_caveat: The source credits k=o(n^(1/4)); fixed-dimensional convergence alone does not answer the growing-dimensional question. Private author-only packet extends the credited coupling under exponential service. Later primary-source leads do not establish novelty.
source: Harchol-Balter: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
why_important: Independence of the queues serving one job in large parallel systems.
where_it_stands: A partial result is recorded in the problem's ledger row; mean-field propagation-of-chaos arguments apply.

title: Sharp approximation ratio for simple alternatives to Gittins
domain_name: Queueing and stochastic networks
statement: Improve or identify the sharp worst-case mean-response approximation factor for M-SERPT or other simple age-based policies in M/G/1.
statement_caveat: The source credits a factor-five guarantee. Heavy-traffic factor-two results and the conjectured sharp factor two are distinct from a uniform all-load guarantee.
source: Harchol-Balter: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
why_important: Sharp approximation factor of simple age-based scheduling policies.
where_it_stands: A constant to identify between known upper and lower bounds.

title: Torus spanning-tree dual homotopy distribution
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Determine the limiting distribution of the homotopy classes of the three edge-simple noncontractible closed paths in the dual complement of a uniform spanning tree on a fine toroidal square grid.
statement_caveat: The question concerns the joint winding information, not only the number of dual cycles. The geometry of the torus is an input. Later line-bundle determinant methods require a separate exact-scope comparison.
source: Schramm: Conformally invariant scaling limits, overview and collection of problems, 2006v2
why_important: Topological observables of the uniform spanning tree on a torus.
where_it_stands: Determinantal and Laplacian methods compute such limits in related cases.

title: Anti-concentration of the determinant of a random Rademacher matrix at non-zero values
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Conjecture 6.8 (Determinant). For any x != 0, P(det M_n = x) <= n^{-(1/2+o(1))n}. (Here M_n is the n x n i.i.d. Rademacher matrix. The source adds that the best current upper bound is exponential [Kahn-Komlos-Szemeredi], and that even the much weaker conjecture that the support of det M_n is super-exponential in size is not known.)
source: Vu: Recent progress in combinatorial random matrix theory
why_important: Anticoncentration of the determinant of a random sign matrix.
where_it_stands: Singularity-probability methods and inverse Littlewood-Offord theory give the tools.

title: Determinantal processes with trigonometric-polynomial symbol as block factors
domain_name: Stationary processes and nonlinear Markov operators
statement: Let f : T -> [0,1] be a trigonometric polynomial of degree m; the stationary determinantal process P_f on Z is m-dependent. Is P_f an (m+1)-block factor of an i.i.d. process? Known for m = 1.
source: Lyons: Determinantal probability, basic properties and conjectures, ICM 2014
why_important: Lyons' question whether an m-dependent determinantal process on Z with a degree-m trigonometric-polynomial symbol is an (m+1)-block factor of an i.i.d. sequence; it joins determinantal structure to the coding theory of finitely dependent processes.
where_it_stands: Known for m = 1. An unaudited attempt at the sublattice case is recorded in the problem's ledger row.

title: Probability that a random Rademacher matrix is normal
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Let nu_n be the probability that M_n (i.i.d. Rademacher entries) is normal, i.e. M M^T = M^T M. Since symmetric matrices are normal, nu_n >= 2^{-(0.5+o(1)) n^2}. Conjecture 9.2 (Normality): nu_n = 2^{-(0.5+o(1)) n^2}. Known: nu_n <= 2^{-(0.302+o(1)) n^2} (Deneanu-Vu); Ferber, Jain and Zhao noted a lemma there can be improved, changing 0.302 'maybe at the 5th decimal place'.
source: Vu: Recent progress in combinatorial random matrix theory
why_important: Probability that a random sign matrix is normal.
where_it_stands: Exponential upper bounds of the right shape are known; the exponent is the target.

title: Quasi-isometry of two independent Poisson point processes on the line
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Are two independent Poisson point processes on R almost surely quasi-isometric to each other (as metric spaces with the induced metric)?
source: Pete: Probability and geometry on groups, lecture notes with open problems
why_important: Coarse geometry of random point sets: are two Poisson processes quasi-isometric?
where_it_stands: One-dimensional, so a combinatorial matching of gap sequences.

title: Expected Lovasz theta of a random circulant graph
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: For the graph on Z/nZ formed by independently including each unordered nonzero generator pair {k,-k} with probability 1/2, is E theta(G)=(1+o(1)) sqrt(n)?
statement_caveat: The inverse-pair convention includes the order-two generator once when n is even; this differs substantively from independent edges.
source: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
why_important: Lovasz theta of a random circulant graph.
where_it_stands: Fourier diagonalisation of circulants reduces it to a random trigonometric problem.

title: Random complex phase-retrieval injectivity at 4M-5 measurements
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Let p_M be the probability that a complex Gaussian (4M-5)-by-M matrix gives an injective phaseless measurement map modulo global phase. Is p_M<1 for each meaningful M, and does p_M tend to zero?
statement_caveat: M>=2 is needed for the matrix size to be meaningful. The two clauses are retained as one source conjecture, not counted twice.
source: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
why_important: Phase retrieval: when is a Gaussian measurement map injective up to phase?
where_it_stands: An algebraic-geometric probability with small cases computable.

title: Worst square-submatrix conditioning in a Gaussian frame
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: For a (2M-1)-by-M matrix of independent standard real Gaussians, determine the asymptotic size of omega(A), the minimum smallest singular value over row subsets whose complement has rank below M. In particular determine whether its decay is exponential and identify the exponential rate.
statement_caveat: Almost surely every M-row subset is nonsingular, so the minimum reduces to M-row subsets. Interpret asymptotic size in probability; the source does not specify a convergence mode or a normalized logarithmic limit.
source: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
why_important: Robust injectivity of Gaussian frames over row subsets.
where_it_stands: Union bounds against small-ball estimates for minimal singular values.

title: A sharp lower bound on the probability that a sum of nonnegative unit-mean variables exceeds its mean plus one
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: Let X_1,...,X_n be independent random variables with X_i >= 0 and E X_i = 1 for every i. Prove or disprove that P(sum_i X_i <= n + 1) >= 1 - 1/e. The source notes that the bound is attained in the limit by the i.i.d. example X_i = n+1 with probability 1/(n+1) and 0 otherwise, for which the probability is 1 - (n/(n+1))^n, decreasing to 1 - 1/e.
source: Bandeira: Ten lectures and forty-two open problems in the mathematics of data science
locator: Open Problem 4.6 and Conjecture 4.33, PDF p. 78
why_important: A classical tail inequality for sums of nonnegative random variables with mean one.
where_it_stands: Moment and decomposition methods give steadily improving constants.

title: Sum of maximum and minimum bisection of a random regular graph
domain_name: Random graphs and networks
statement: Let G be a uniformly random d-regular graph on n vertices. Prove or disprove that for every d, as n grows, (1/n)(MaxBis(G) + MinBis(G)) = d/2 + o(1), where MaxBis and MinBis are the maximum and minimum bisection sizes. The source notes that the conjecture is known to hold up to o(sqrt(d)) terms by Dembo-Montanari-Sen.
source: Bandeira: Ten lectures and forty-two open problems in the mathematics of data science
locator: Open Problem 8.5 and Conjecture 8.5, PDF p. 117
why_important: Maximum and minimum bisections of random regular graphs.
where_it_stands: Spin-glass interpolation methods handle large degree; the identity is a sharp target.

title: Convergence threshold for the projected power method in the spiked Wigner model
domain_name: Optimal transport, statistics and inference
statement: In the synchronisation model Y = z z^T + sigma W with z in {-1,+1}^n and W a Wigner matrix, for which values of sigma does the projected power method converge to the optimal solution of the maximum-likelihood problem, or at least to a solution correlating well with z, with high probability?
source: Bandeira: Ten lectures and forty-two open problems in the mathematics of data science
why_important: When does the projected power method reach the optimum in group synchronisation?
where_it_stands: Spectral initialisation plus a contraction argument in a fixed Gaussian model.

title: Consistency of the maximum likelihood estimator for multireference alignment
domain_name: Optimal transport, statistics and inference
statement: (1) Is the quasi-maximum-likelihood (or the maximum-likelihood) estimator consistent for the multireference alignment problem, after fixing the power spectrum appropriately? (2) For a given signal length L and noise level sigma, how large must the number of observations n be to allow reasonably accurate recovery in the multireference alignment problem?
source: Bandeira: Ten lectures and forty-two open problems in the mathematics of data science
why_important: Consistency of maximum likelihood for multireference alignment.
where_it_stands: Moment-tensor methods settled the sample complexity; consistency is the remaining step.

title: Correlations of critical-tree leaves at mesoscopic separation
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: For two leaves separated by r_n positions in the cyclic interval representation, prove that their continuous-height correlation tends to1-alpha when log(r_n)/log(n) tends to alpha in[0,1].
statement_caveat: The macroscopic alpha=1 case is already established in the corrected published Aldous-Pittel result. All separation exponents form one question, not separate variants.
source: Aldous-Janson: Critical beta-splitting random tree II, overview and open problems
why_important: Height correlations in Aldous's beta-splitting random tree.
where_it_stands: Explicit recursions for the model are available.

title: The multifractal spectrum of extremal ray local times
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: Determine the Hausdorff dimension of rays with limsup, or liminf, N_ray^n/n^2=a under Theorem1.6(ii).
statement_caveat: All a and the related limsup/liminf spectra form one source question. Dimension uses the usual generation ultrametric on the tree boundary.
source: Aidekon-Hu-Shi: Boundedness of discounted tree sums
why_important: Open question 3 of Aidekon, Hu and Shi on discounted tree sums: the Hausdorff dimension of the rays whose local times grow at a prescribed quadratic rate.
where_it_stands: The quadratic growth is Theorem 1.6(ii) of the source (2024); the spectrum asks for the standard multifractal analysis on the boundary of the tree.

title: Convergence of the variance of the stochastic travelling salesman tour length
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: In the travelling salesman problem for n uniformly distributed points in [0,1]^2, prove that the variance of the length of the optimal tour converges to a constant as n tends to infinity, and identify this constant if possible. Chatterjee attributes the conjecture to Mike Steele.
source: Chatterjee: A general method for lower bounds on fluctuations of random variables
why_important: Second-order behaviour of the random travelling salesman tour.
where_it_stands: A matching lower bound technique exists; the limit of the variance is the target.

title: Tight fluctuation lower bound for Euclidean minimal matching
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: Prove a tight lower bound for the fluctuations of the length of the minimal matching when the points are uniformly distributed in [0,1]^d.
source: Chatterjee: A general method for lower bounds on fluctuations of random variables
why_important: Lower bounds for fluctuations of random Euclidean matching.
where_it_stands: Methods that give the assignment-problem bound transfer.

title: Brownian limit and correlation for the meander lattice walk
domain_name: Gaussian fields, LQG and planar maps
statement: Prove that the lattice walk Z arising in the meander problem converges to a two-dimensional Brownian motion whose coordinate correlation is -cos(pi gamma^2 / 4) for the appropriate gamma. A solution would, by an argument analogous to Gwynne-Sun's estimate of the FK partition function, give the exponent alpha in the asymptotic enumeration of meanders. The source carries an UPDATE stating that, contrary to the conjecture, the scaling limit of a uniform meander is expected to be LQG with central charge c = -4 decorated by two independent SLE_8 curves, with kappa not equal to 16/gamma^2, so that the mating-of-trees results do not apply directly.
source: Gwynne, Holden, Sun: Mating of trees for random planar maps and LQG, a survey
why_important: Meanders and their conjectured link to Liouville quantum gravity.
where_it_stands: Mating-of-trees encodings give a concrete walk whose limit is the target.

title: Strong convergence of modular-group actions on finite projective lines
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Does the PSL_2(Z) action on P^1(F_q), restricted to constants-orthogonal vectors, converge strongly to the regular group representation for every fixed tuple of integer matrices?
statement_caveat: The diffusion-operator formulation and arbitrary-polynomial formulation are equivalent in the source and are counted once. Random homomorphisms from C2*C3 are a different model.
source: The strong convergence phenomenon,2025 survey
why_important: Strong convergence for an arithmetic action, a spectral-gap question.
where_it_stands: The polynomial method proves strong convergence for related random actions.

title: Largest coefficient dimension compatible with strong convergence
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Determine the optimal growth of matrix-coefficient dimension D_N for strong convergence of polynomials in Gaussian or Haar random matrices.
statement_caveat: Known subexponential sufficiency and failure at sufficiently large exp(C*N^2) leave a gap; Gaussian and Haar versions are grouped. New q-Gaussian model statements are not automatically the same fixed-model question.
source: The strong convergence phenomenon,2025 survey
why_important: How large matrix coefficients can be in strong convergence theorems.
where_it_stands: Current methods give explicit dimension bounds to improve.

title: Joint strong convergence for permutation and deterministic matrices
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Develop a permutation-matrix counterpart of joint strong convergence with strongly convergent deterministic matrices.
statement_caveat: Removing the common constant vector of permutation matrices requires an explicit convention for deterministic matrices that do not preserve its orthogonal complement.
source: The strong convergence phenomenon,2025 survey
why_important: Strong convergence for permutation matrices with deterministic coefficients.
where_it_stands: The Gaussian and unitary versions are proved.

title: Separation of two peaks in random square-grid labelings
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: Uniformly label an n-by-n square grid and condition on exactly two local maxima. Does their graph distance divided by n converge in distribution to zero?
statement_caveat: This is the literal displayed question, despite the heading about repulsion. Verify against Twin peaks (2020) before correcting the sign or reporting a counterexample.
source: Krzysztof Burdzy: My favorite open problems
why_important: Geometry of random fields conditioned on few local maxima.
where_it_stands: A concrete scaling question on a finite grid.

title: Synchronous reflection outside a disk
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE
statement: For synchronously coupled reflected Brownian motions in the exterior of a nondegenerate closed disk, can their distance have positive limsup with positive probability?
statement_caveat: This unbounded exterior geometry differs from the bounded-domain existence question.
source: Krzysztof Burdzy: My favorite open problems
why_important: Long-term behaviour of synchronously coupled reflected Brownian motions.
where_it_stands: A two-dimensional exterior domain with explicit geometry.

title: Efficient reflected-Brownian coupling in acute triangles
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE
statement: In any acute triangle, can reflected Brownian motions from distinct starting points be coupled so their meeting-time tail decays at every exponential rate strictly below the first positive Neumann spectral rate?
statement_caveat: Check the generator convention in Burdzy-Kendall (2000): the page calls its rate a Laplacian eigenvalue. A factor-two convention discrepancy is not a solution of the coupling question.
source: Krzysztof Burdzy: My favorite open problems
why_important: Efficient couplings of reflected Brownian motion in triangles.
where_it_stands: Spectral theory of triangles and coupling constructions are developed.

title: Is the uniform distribution on a convex body in R^d completely mixable of order d+1?
domain_name: Optimal transport, statistics and inference
statement: Let C be a convex set in R^d. Is the uniform distribution on C necessarily n-CM for every n >= d+1? The source states the problem is equivalent to (d+1)-complete mixability and records only the trivial cases d=0 and d=1.
source: Current open questions in complete mixability
why_important: Joint mixability, the core of worst-case risk aggregation bounds.
where_it_stands: A convex-geometric question with the one-dimensional case solved.

title: Is every absolutely continuous law on a bounded interval n-completely mixable for all large n?
domain_name: Optimal transport, statistics and inference
statement: Puccetti, Wang and Wang show that a law on [a,b] with density f(x) >= 3/(n(b-a)) is n-CM, so any absolutely continuous law with a density bounded away from zero is n-CM for all large n. Can the lower bound on the density be dropped: is every absolutely continuous distribution on a bounded interval n-CM for all sufficiently large n?
source: Current open questions in complete mixability
why_important: Sharp density conditions for complete mixability.
where_it_stands: Constructive; the known sufficient bound is explicit.

title: Extra conditions making a unimodal law on a bounded interval completely mixable
domain_name: Optimal transport, statistics and inference
statement: Counterexamples are known showing that the mean condition a + (b-a)/n <= mu <= b - (b-a)/n is not sufficient for the complete mixability of a law with a unimodal density on a bounded interval. Under what extra conditions is a unimodal distribution on a bounded interval n-CM? The case of interest is when one of the inequalities in the mean condition is an equality.
source: Current open questions in complete mixability
why_important: Complete mixability of unimodal laws.
where_it_stands: Constructive; known counterexamples mark the boundary.

title: The golden-mean conjecture: mu(G) >= phi for every cubic transitive graph
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Is it the case that mu(G) >= phi = (1 + sqrt 5)/2 for every G in G_3, the class of infinite, connected, transitive, simple, cubic graphs? Known in various classes including TLF-planar graphs; the best general lower bounds are mu >= x with 1/x^2 + 1/x^3 = 1/sqrt 2 for girth at least 3 and mu >= 12^{1/6} for girth at least 4.
source: Grimmett and Li: Self-avoiding walks and connective constants
why_important: A universal lower bound for connective constants of cubic graphs.
where_it_stands: Proved for several large classes of transitive cubic graphs.

title: The sqrt(Delta - 1) lower bound for the connective constant of non-simple transitive multigraphs of degree at least 5
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Theorem 2.1 states that an infinite, connected, Delta-regular, transitive, loopless multigraph with Delta >= 2 satisfies mu(G) >= sqrt(Delta - 1) if either (a) G is simple or (b) G is non-simple and Delta <= 4. Is the same true in the non-simple case with Delta >= 5?
source: Grimmett and Li: Self-avoiding walks and connective constants
why_important: Connective-constant lower bounds for regular multigraphs.
where_it_stands: Proved in the simple-graph and other cases by the source.

title: Removing the log^2 n factor from the fast-phase toppling bound
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Improve the estimate P(T <= kappa n log^2 n) >= 1 - n^{-delta} of (6.3) to one without the log^2 n term, i.e. to a bound of order n.
source: Rolla: Activated random walks on Z^d, survey with open problems
locator: Second Open Problem after Theorem 6.1, Section 6, PDF p. 30
why_important: Linear fixation time for activated random walk.
where_it_stands: The bound with a squared logarithm is proved; the logarithm is the target.

title: Small-sleep-rate behaviour of the critical density for unbiased walks on Z^2
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Theorem 7.2 of the source proves, for transient (d > 2) walks, that zeta_c < 1 for every lambda < infinity AND that zeta_c tends to 0 as lambda tends to 0. Prove a similar statement for unbiased walks on Z^2.
source: Rolla: Activated random walks on Z^d, survey with open problems
locator: First Open Problem after Theorem 7.2, Section 7, PDF p. 35
why_important: Activated random walk with recurrent walks at low sleep rate.
where_it_stands: The transient case is proved in the source.

title: A finite-graph approximation to frozen percolation on the three-regular tree
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: Show that the canonical frozen-percolation process on the three-regular tree is the local weak limit of a suitable sequence of finite graphs.
statement_caveat: This asks for finite graphs, not the known growing-cluster-threshold approximation on an infinite binary tree.
source: Frozen percolation on the binary tree is nonendogenous
why_important: Frozen percolation on finite graphs as an approximation of the tree model.
where_it_stands: Endogeny of the tree model is known; local convergence is the step.

title: All bivariate frozen-percolation fixed points and their attraction domains
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: Classify every fixed point and domain of attraction of d(mu_h)/dh=T2(mu_h)-mu_h for frozen percolation on the oriented binary tree.
statement_caveat: The two scale-invariant fixed points are known; this question permits nonscale-invariant couplings and asks for their dynamics.
source: Frozen percolation on the binary tree is nonendogenous
why_important: Fixed points of the frozen-percolation evolution equation.
where_it_stands: An explicit equation on laws of one variable.

title: Biased random square-lattice orientations
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Does every nonzero orientation bias give positive probability of an infinite directed path from the origin?
source: Selected problems in probability theory
why_important: Directed paths under biased orientations.
where_it_stands: A sharp question with monotonicity and coupling tools.

title: Concavity of the entropy of determinantal measures in the kernel
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: For positive contractions Q_1, Q_2 on l^2(E), E finite, Ent(P_{(Q_1+Q_2)/2}) >= (Ent(P_{Q_1}) + Ent(P_{Q_2}))/2; which implies (Conjecture 5.3, by finite restrictions) concavity of the entropy rate H(P_f) of stationary determinantal processes in the symbol f; the converse is not claimed.
source: Lyons: Determinantal probability, basic properties and conjectures, ICM 2014
why_important: Concavity of entropy for determinantal measures.
where_it_stands: Finite-dimensional matrix inequality; checked in small cases.

title: Coupling of determinantal projection measures with union marginal
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Given H = H_1 (+) H_2 orthogonal in l^2(E), is there a coupling of P_{H_1} and P_{H_2} whose union has law P_H?
source: Lyons: Determinantal probability, basic properties and conjectures, ICM 2014
why_important: Couplings of determinantal processes for orthogonal sums.
where_it_stands: Finite ground sets; known in special cases.

title: d-bar distance bound for commuting versus general equivariant kernels
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: For Gamma-equivariant positive contractions Q, Q' the bound d-bar(P_Q, P_{Q'}) <= 6 3^{2/3} ||Q - Q'||_1^{1/3} holds, and d-bar(P_Q, P_{Q'}) <= ||Q - Q'||_1 when Q and Q' commute. Does the linear bound d-bar <= ||Q - Q'||_1 hold for all pairs?
source: Lyons: Determinantal probability, basic properties and conjectures, ICM 2014
why_important: Optimal transport distance between equivariant determinantal processes.
where_it_stands: A Lipschitz bound with a cube-root version proved.

title: Cutoff for cyclic-to-random transpositions
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Does the shuffle that swaps the cyclically chosen position with a uniform random position have cutoff?
statement_caveat: This is a time-inhomogeneous deck chain or a chain sampled by full sweeps. It differs from the cyclic adjacent-transposition shuffle, whose cutoff was proved by Nam-Nestoridi.
source: Levin-Peres: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition
why_important: Cutoff for the cyclic-to-random transposition shuffle.
where_it_stands: The mixing order is known; cutoff needs the matching lower bound.

title: Cutoff for card-cyclic random insertion
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Does the shuffle that cyclically chooses a card label, removes that card and reinserts it uniformly have cutoff?
statement_caveat: Random-to-random insertion is a different shuffle and is resolved. Here the selected label, rather than its present position, advances cyclically.
source: Levin-Peres: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition
why_important: Cutoff for the cyclic remove-and-insert shuffle.
where_it_stands: Same structure as the previous shuffle, with known order of mixing.

title: Mixing exponent of uniform binary row additions
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Determine the mixing order for the walk on GL_N(2) that adds one uniformly chosen distinct row to another.
statement_caveat: The same question on the Peres author page is counted once. The book phrase saying order2^N nodes is a typo; the group size is of order2^(N^2). The asymptotic question concerns N tending to infinity.
source: Levin-Peres: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition
locator: Chapter26 Question9, PDFp377; Peres current page Question2
why_important: Mixing time of row-addition walk on GL_N(2).
where_it_stands: Comparison techniques give bounds of nearby orders.

title: Time regularization in Hilbert spaces: Let X0 be a Hilbert space
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE
statement: Problem 6. (Time regularization in Hilbert spaces) Let X0 be a Hilbert space. Does the regularization result of Theorem 5.7 extend to p = 2 in the critical case (i.e. equality in (6.1) holds for some j)? Stochastic reaction-diﬀusion equations In Subsections 8.2 we discussed the global well-posedness of some coercive systems. We also included a non- coercive case in Subsection 8.2.3, where a predator-prey model was discussed. Some triangular models we are able to treat as well (see [14] for the Brussela- tor and Gray-Scott model both with cubic f).
source: Agresti-Veraar: Nonlinear SPDEs and maximal regularity,published NoDEA2025
why_important: Critical time regularisation for stochastic PDEs in Hilbert spaces.
where_it_stands: The non-critical and p>2 cases are proved in the source.

title: Reaction-diﬀusion with triangular structure: Let O be Td or Rd and ℓ≥2
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE
statement: Problem 7. (Reaction-diﬀusion with triangular structure) Let O be Td or Rd and ℓ≥2. Consider the reaction-diﬀusion system (8.14) with (bn,i)n≥1 ∈ Cγ(O; ℓ2) for some γ > 0 and with possibly additional boundary conditions in case O ̸= Td. Does global well-posedness hold for the reaction-diﬀusion system (8.14) under the following conditions for a ﬁxed h > 1 and each i ∈{1, . . .
source: Agresti-Veraar: Nonlinear SPDEs and maximal regularity,published NoDEA2025
why_important: Global well-posedness for stochastic reaction-diffusion with triangular structure.
where_it_stands: The critical-space framework of the source covers the related systems.

title: Exact minimum stationary cover time for reversible chains
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Prove or refute E_pi C>=(n-1)H_(n-1) for every irreducible reversible discrete-time chain on n states.
statement_caveat: The comparison is the nonlazy complete graph. Feige asymptotic lower bounds for unweighted graphs do not establish this exact weighted-chain statement.
source: Aldous-Fill: Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, 2002 recompiled2014
why_important: Aldous-Fill cover-time lower bound for reversible chains.
where_it_stands: Extremal for the complete graph; known for large classes of chains.

title: Asymptotic uniformity of the final discovered vertex
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For simple random walk from a fixed vertex on growing finite vertex-transitive graphs, does the law of the last new vertex approach the uniform law in total variation?
statement_caveat: Uniform stationary initialization makes the marginal exactly uniform by symmetry, but that is weaker than the fixed-start question.
source: Aldous-Fill: Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, 2002 recompiled2014
why_important: Is the last new vertex of a random walk nearly uniform on transitive graphs?
where_it_stands: Known in specific families; coupling and hitting-time estimates.

title: Mixing of the random-pair binary crossover chain
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For K even binary words of length L, repeatedly choose a uniform pairing and independently swap each paired coordinate with probability1/2. Prove the proposed O(log K*log L) mixing bound within each fixed column-sum class.
statement_caveat: The source uses a family of words and a fresh uniform permutation to place pairs; shared pairings couple the columns. Replace logarithms by log(K+1),log(L+1) when stating small-parameter bounds. General evolutionary algorithms are different chains.
source: Aldous-Fill: Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, 2002 recompiled2014
why_important: Mixing of a random pairing-swap process on binary words.
where_it_stands: A concrete bound to prove by coupling.

title: Mixing of gap-jump exclusion on a discrete circle
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: For m particles on K circular sites, choose a vacant site and a direction by the source per-step rule, then move the first encountered particle to the site. Prove the conjectured tau2=Theta(m^3) and tau1=O(m^3 log m) uniformly in K>m.
statement_caveat: The step first chooses a site uniformly from all K, doing nothing if occupied. The continuum-circle limit keeps m fixed before K grows; both spectral and mixing targets are grouped.
source: Aldous-Fill: Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, 2002 recompiled2014
why_important: A conjectured stationary law for a circular particle model.
where_it_stands: Explicit finite state space; matrix-product methods.

title: Competitive exclusion in the two-type contact process with unequal death rates
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: In the two-species competition model (a multitype contact process with birth rates beta_i and death rates delta_i), show that species 1 outcompetes species 2 when the two dispersal distributions are the same and beta_1/delta_1 > beta_2/delta_2. Durrett notes that this is what the Competitive Exclusion Principle predicts and that simulation supports it.
source: Durrett: Coexistence in stochastic spatial models (Wald lectures)
why_important: Competition between species in a multitype contact process.
where_it_stands: Voter-model perturbation results cover nearby parameter regions.

title: Absence of coexistence in the two-type colicin model with equal death rates
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: In the colicin model of Durrett and Levin (type 1 produces colicin, which raises the death rate of type 2 by an amount proportional to the local density of 1s), show that coexistence is not possible when lambda_1 < lambda_2 and delta_1 = delta_2 = 1. Durrett notes that in the parameter range where the mean-field ODE has an interior fixed point that fixed point is unstable, and that simulations show segregation with the interface moving in favour of the 1s.
source: Durrett: Coexistence in stochastic spatial models (Wald lectures)
why_important: Coexistence in the colicin model.
where_it_stands: Same perturbative approach; mean-field behaviour is known.

title: Uniqueness for the one-dimensional short-range Riesz Gibbs gas
domain_name: Statistical mechanics: polymers, gases, interfaces
statement: Establish the expected uniqueness of the one-dimensional short-range Riesz Gibbs state in the unresolved exponent range1<s<=2.
statement_caveat: The s>2 uniqueness regime is already known. Boursier proves a unique thermodynamic limit of the circular finite-volume laws for s>1, which is not by itself uniqueness among all DLR Gibbs states.
source: Lewin: Coulomb and Riesz gases, the known and the unknown,2022
why_important: Uniqueness of the one-dimensional short-range Riesz Gibbs state.
where_it_stands: Uniqueness is known for larger exponents; the range 1<s<=2 is the gap.

title: Optimal odd functions for many-player correlation distillation
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: When r independent noisy copies of a common uniform bit string use the same odd Boolean function, is the agreement probability maximized by majority on some odd subset of coordinates?
statement_caveat: The number of players and the noise parameter are one optimization problem. This differs from two-party erasure distillation and from minimizing threshold stability.
source: O Donnell: Open problems in analysis of Boolean functions
locator: PDF p.6, Optimality of Majorities for Non-Interactive Correlation Distillation
why_important: Optimal non-interactive correlation distillation.
where_it_stands: Hypercontractivity and partial results cover small numbers of players.

title: Minimum correlation of symmetric Gaussian sets
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: For correlated standard Gaussian vectors with prescribed rho and set measures mu,nu, minimize P(X in A,Y in B) under central symmetry A=-A.
statement_caveat: The proposed centered-ball optimizer is not the general optimization question. Heilman1511.00382 gives negative results for ball/complement maximizers in dimension at least2; this does not identify every optimum.
source: O Donnell: Open problems in analysis of Boolean functions
why_important: Gaussian noise stability under central symmetry.
where_it_stands: Symmetric isoperimetry has partial results; finite-dimensional reductions exist.

title: Optimal limited independence for Gaussian polynomial thresholds
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: Determine the smallest k(d,epsilon) for which every k-wise independent standard-Gaussian vector fools every degree-d polynomial threshold to error epsilon.
statement_caveat: The joint distribution of every k coordinates must be product Gaussian. Matching finitely many mixed moments alone is a weaker property and is not substituted for this assumption.
source: O Donnell: Open problems in analysis of Boolean functions
locator: PDF p.9, k-wise Independence for PTFs
why_important: Bounded independence fooling polynomial threshold functions.
where_it_stands: Known for low degree; the dependence on d and epsilon is the target.

title: Which beta-ensembles admit the nesting coupling of tridiagonal minors?
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: The top minors of the tridiagonal beta-Hermite model give a coupling of beta-ensembles of different sizes (a nested family). Can any other Dyson beta-ensembles be coupled this way? What about other natural random matrix models?
source: Virag: Operator limits of random matrices (ICM 2014)
why_important: Couplings of beta ensembles of different sizes.
where_it_stands: Explicit tridiagonal models give one coupling.

title: Higher-order edge limits are the operators -d^2/dt^2 + t^{1/(2k+1)} + (2/sqrt beta) t^{-k/(2k+1)} b'
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: When the equilibrium density vanishes at the edge like x^{2k+1/2} rather than x^{1/2}, the tridiagonal matrices T_n should converge, after scaling, to the random operator S_{beta,k} = -d^2/dt^2 + t^{1/(2k+1)} + (2/sqrt beta) t^{-k/(2k+1)} b'_t, where b' is white noise. For beta = 2 the eigenvalue limits have been studied by Riemann-Hilbert methods.
source: Virag: Operator limits of random matrices (ICM 2014)
why_important: Operator limits at non-generic spectral edges.
where_it_stands: The stochastic Airy method extends to modified edge behaviour.

title: Deriving the gap Painleve equation from the Brownian carousel generator
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Can one deduce the Painleve equation for the bulk gap probability from the PDEs corresponding to the generator of the Brownian carousel SDE?
source: Virag: Operator limits of random matrices (ICM 2014)
locator: Question 9 (Painleve in the bulk), PDF p. 25
why_important: Painleve equations from the Brownian carousel.
where_it_stands: The carousel SDE and its generator are explicit.

title: A rho-mixing, bilaterally deterministic, finite-state stationary sequence
domain_name: Stationary processes and nonlinear Markov operators
statement: Does there exist a nondegenerate strictly stationary, finite-state, rho-mixing, bilaterally deterministic sequence X = (X_k, k in Z)? (Bilaterally deterministic: the sequence is measurable with respect to its double tail sigma-field, modulo null sets.)
source: Bradley: Basic properties of strong mixing conditions, a survey and some open questions
why_important: Existence question in classical strong-mixing theory.
where_it_stands: A construction problem in a finite-state setting.

title: A psi-mixing or 1-dependent sequence that is not a function of a Harris recurrent Markov chain
domain_name: Stationary processes and nonlinear Markov operators
statement: Does there exist a strictly stationary psi-mixing (or perhaps even 1-dependent) sequence which cannot be represented as an instantaneous function of a strictly stationary, Harris recurrent Markov chain?
source: Bradley: Basic properties of strong mixing conditions, a survey and some open questions
why_important: Representation of psi-mixing sequences by Harris chains.
where_it_stands: Construction or obstruction in a concrete class.

title: Spectral characterisation of rho*-mixing for stationary Gaussian sequences
domain_name: Stationary processes and nonlinear Markov operators
statement: What condition on a spectral density is necessary and sufficient for a stationary Gaussian sequence to be rho*-mixing?
source: Bradley: Basic properties of strong mixing conditions, a survey and some open questions
why_important: Spectral characterisation of rho-star mixing for Gaussian sequences.
where_it_stands: The rho-mixing analogue is classical.

title: Uniqueness of the unbounded major-road component
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Must the major-road set E(infinity,1) of every SIRSN have only one unbounded connected component almost surely?
statement_caveat: Disconnected finite major-road pieces are allowed by definition. The question concerns unbounded components only.
source: Aldous: Scale-invariant random spatial networks
why_important: Structure of scale-invariant random spatial networks.
where_it_stands: The network is constructed explicitly; one-component questions are tractable.

title: Asymptotic total length of finite SIRSN samples
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: For k uniform points in a square of area k, prove that the mean total length of their spanning route network is asymptotic to ell*k.
statement_caveat: Length includes route pieces outside the sampling square. This global excursion contribution is the main source obstruction.
source: Aldous: Scale-invariant random spatial networks
why_important: Length asymptotics of route networks on random points.
where_it_stands: Subadditivity arguments give the limit constant.

title: Entropic repulsion for the continuous solid-on-solid interaction
domain_name: Statistical mechanics: polymers, gases, interfaces
statement: Open Problem 5. Prove similar results (even without the proper constants) when V(x) is not uniformly strictly convex. In particular prove it for the continuous SOS model, that is, the continuous effective interface model with interaction V(x) = |x|. Note that the behavior should be different as soon as the tail of V changes. This has important impact on other related issues, as is discussed in Sections 4 and 6. ['Similar results' refers to the entropic repulsion heights of Section 3.2: sqrt(4 g_d log N)-type heights in d >= 3 and the two-dimensional statement (20).] Setting of the source (Section 1): effective interface model phi = (phi_i)_{i in Lambda} in R^Lambda with Hamiltonian sum over nearest neighbours of V(phi_i - phi_j) and zero boundary condition; 'Gaussian' means V(x) = x^2/2, 'uniformly strictly convex' means c_- <= V'' <= c_+; the repelled (hard-wall) measure P^+ conditions on phi_i >= 0 on a subbox; the DG (discrete Gaussian) model is the integer-valued version.
source: Velenik: Localization and delocalization of random interfaces (Probab. Surveys 2006)
why_important: Interface behaviour for non-convex gradient models.
where_it_stands: Results for strictly convex interactions are known; the continuous SOS model is the test case.

title: Height of the two-dimensional field pinned at the origin and kept positive, for convex interactions
domain_name: Statistical mechanics: polymers, gases, interfaces
statement: Open Problem 6. Extend (21) (when d = 2) to the case of uniformly strictly convex interactions V. [(21), same page: for the field pinned at the origin and conditioned to be positive, E^+_{Z^2 \ {0}}(phi_i) is of order sqrt(|i|) for d = 1 and of order log|i| for d = 2; the source adds that the two-dimensional result has only been established for the Gaussian model, and that an extension to uniformly strictly convex V would also allow an extension of the results of [29], discussed in Section 6, to this class.] Setting of the source (Section 1): effective interface model phi = (phi_i)_{i in Lambda} in R^Lambda with Hamiltonian sum over nearest neighbours of V(phi_i - phi_j) and zero boundary condition; 'Gaussian' means V(x) = x^2/2, 'uniformly strictly convex' means c_- <= V'' <= c_+; the repelled (hard-wall) measure P^+ conditions on phi_i >= 0 on a subbox; the DG (discrete Gaussian) model is the integer-valued version.
source: Velenik: Localization and delocalization of random interfaces (Probab. Surveys 2006)
why_important: Entropic repulsion with convex interactions in two dimensions.
where_it_stands: The Gaussian case is known.

title: Conjecture 11.8 (Front-Markov property, full saturated regime) of arXiv:2608.15987
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: "In the full saturated regime — without the dissipative condition κ<1 of (6), and uniformly through the critical window — there is a constant C such that, for the cluster law in G_n, d_TV(L(failed cluster), L(multitype GW with M)) ≤ C(ε(δ)+η_n), with η_n→0 as G_n →^BS T and ε(δ)→0 as the saturation margin δ→∞. Equivalently, the cascade front is asymptotically Markov: conditional on the set of failed vertices at generation k and their types, the failures into generation k+1 are asymptotically independent of generations <k."
locator: Conjecture 11.8 (Front-Markov property, full saturated regime); Section 11.5, "The remaining conjecture"
why_important: Front asymptotics in a saturated branching system through the critical window.
where_it_stands: Proved in the dissipative regime by the source.

title: Open problem (3), "Sharp moment hypotheses for the CRT limit" of arXiv:2608.15987
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: "Reduce the exponential-moment hypothesis of Theorem 6.4 to g''(1)<∞; see Remark 6.5."
locator: Open problem (3), "Sharp moment hypotheses for the CRT limit"; Section 12.3
why_important: Sharp moment hypothesis for a branching limit theorem.
where_it_stands: A technical weakening suggested by the source.

title: Joint law of neighboring ideal Voronoi vertices
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Find the joint distribution of all neighboring vertices viewed from a typical vertex of the hyperbolic IPVT.
statement_caveat: Typical means the vertex Palm law, not the cell containing a fixed point. The source gives Gamma(d+1) separation at a typical vertex.
source: D Achille Curien Enriquez Lyons Unel: Ideal Poisson Voronoi tessellations on hyperbolic spaces
why_important: Local structure of the hyperbolic ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation.
where_it_stands: Explicit Poisson geometry in the hyperbolic plane.

title: Low-intensity variance of typical hyperbolic Voronoi cell volume
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Determine the finite limit, if any, of lambda times the typical-cell volume variance at actual nucleus intensity lambda, and its proposed coupling representation.
statement_caveat: Use lambda for the actual intensity in this entry. The source uses an auxiliary reparametrization in parts of its proofs; no reparametrized intensity is substituted in the Palm identity.
source: D Achille Curien Enriquez Lyons Unel: Ideal Poisson Voronoi tessellations on hyperbolic spaces
why_important: Typical-cell volume variance of ideal Voronoi tessellations.
where_it_stands: A limit with a proposed coupling representation.

title: Escape probability of a transient one-dimensional excited random walk
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing

source: Kosygina and Zerner: Excited random walks, results, methods, open problems, 2012
why_important: Escape probability of transient excited random walk.

title: Zero velocity on the non-transient event for excited random walks
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing

title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for Ulam's ergodic theorem for general Volterra operators
domain_name: Stationary processes and nonlinear Markov operators

title: Trajectories of quadratic bistochastic operators
domain_name: Stationary processes and nonlinear Markov operators
statement: A quadratic operator V on S^{m-1} is bistochastic if V(x) is majorised by x for every x, i.e. the partial sums of the decreasing rearrangement of V(x) are dominated by those of x. Investigate the behaviour of the trajectories of the bistochastic quadratic operators.
source: Rozikov: Quadratic stochastic operators, results and open problems
why_important: Structure of bistochastic quadratic stochastic operators.
where_it_stands: Majorisation gives a finite-dimensional problem.

title: The bubble hypothesis for the backbone of the Brownian net
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE
statement: Let N be the graph of the backbone of the Brownian net (paths started at time -infinity), S and M the sets of separation points and meeting points on N, S* = S union {(*,-infinity)}, M* = M union {(*,infinity)}, and phi: S* -> M*, phi(z) = the first meeting point of the left-most and right-most paths starting at z (phi(z) = (*,infinity) if they never meet), with phi: M* -> S* defined analogously by time reversal. Conjecture 8.1 (Bubble hypothesis) (a) Almost surely, there does not exist an infinite sequence of points (z_k)_{k>=0} in S* union M*, all different from each other, such that phi(z_{k-1}) = z_k for all k >= 1. (b) Almost surely, there does not exist an infinite sequence of points (z_k) in S* union M*, all different, such that phi(z_k) = z_{k-1} for all k >= 1.
source: Schertzer, Sun, Swart: The Brownian web, the Brownian net, and their universality
why_important: Fine structure of the Brownian net.
where_it_stands: The net is constructed with special points classified.

title: Local finiteness of potential most recent common ancestors in the Brownian net
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE
statement: For the Brownian web, let M be the set of all first meeting points of pairs of paths started at time 0, M := {(x,t) in R^2: t > 0, exist pi, pi' in W({0} x R) with pi(t) = x = pi'(t), pi < pi' on (0,t)}, interpreted as most recent common ancestors; it is easy to see that M is a locally finite subset of R x (0, infinity). Conjecture 8.3 (Potential most recent common ancestors). If we replace W({0} x R) in (8.3) by N({0} x R), the set of all Brownian net paths started at time 0, then the set M is a locally finite subset of R x (0, infinity).
source: Schertzer, Sun, Swart: The Brownian web, the Brownian net, and their universality
locator: Conjecture 8.3 (Potential most recent common ancestors), Section 8.2, PDF p. 72
why_important: Meeting points of the Brownian web.
where_it_stands: Special-point classification for the web is developed.

title: Hunt's hypothesis for a product of two independent Levy processes
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE
statement: Let X_1 and X_2 be independent Levy processes on R^n and R^m respectively, both satisfying Hunt's hypothesis (H). Does the R^{n+m}-valued Levy process X = (X_1, X_2) satisfy (H)? Equivalently (Question 4): if S is a nonempty proper subspace of R^n and the projections X_S and X_{S-perp} are independent and both satisfy (H), does X satisfy (H)?
source: Hunt's hypothesis (H) for Markov processes: survey and beyond
why_important: Potential theory of products of Levy processes.

title: Hunt's hypothesis for pure jump subordinators with infinite Levy measure
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE
statement: Does any pure jump subordinator with infinite Levy measure satisfy Hunt's hypothesis (H)? More generally, does any pure jump n-dimensional Levy process satisfy (H)? The survey records in Section 2 that it is still unknown whether any pure jump subordinator of type-(alpha, beta) satisfies (H), where a pure jump subordinator is of type-(alpha, beta) with 0 < alpha < beta < 1 if its Levy measure has a density nu with c^{-1} x^{-(1+alpha)} <= nu(x) <= c x^{-(1+beta)} for x in (0,1].
source: Hunt's hypothesis (H) for Markov processes: survey and beyond
why_important: Getoor's question for pure-jump subordinators.
where_it_stands: Known for several classes of subordinators.

title: Is Hunt's hypothesis stable under independent sums of Levy processes?
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE

source: Hunt's hypothesis (H) for Markov processes: survey and beyond
why_important: Stability of Hunt's hypothesis under sums.

title: Non-Poisson low-intensity ideal Voronoi diagrams
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs

title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for an Lp quantile-process limit
domain_name: Optimal transport, statistics and inference

domain_name: Optimal transport, statistics and inference

statement_caveat: The empirical plan is almost surely a map, but the population problem has many optimal couplings. The task is to identify the plan selected by empirical optimization, not merely its limiting cost2.

title: Order of the expected waiting time for a scale-indexed family of discrete patterns
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: Given for each n a collection A_n of patterns of length n, what is the order of the expected waiting time E T(A_n) until some element of A_n is observed in a simple random walk? The source notes it is aware of no previous study of pattern problems in which a natural definition of the collection of patterns is made for each n.

title: Infinitely many fixed points of a finite-color automaton
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: For a finite color set of size at least3 and a deterministic child-count automaton under the paper standing offspring assumptions, can the distributional map have infinitely many fixed points?

title: Law of large numbers and constants for NUV lengths
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Prove existence and identify the linear-scale NUV length constants in the source Euclidean, iid-weighted-grid and complete-graph mean-field models.

title: Rough-path continuity of chronological loop attachment
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE
statement: Prove appropriate Holder, p-variation, or rough-path continuity estimates for the chronological loop-attachment map, possibly restricted to the cusp conditions proposed by the authors.

title: Hamiltonicity of the random graph with minimum degree three above edge density three halves
domain_name: Random graphs and networks
statement: We now consider conditioning on minimum degree at least three. Let L_c = lim_{n -> infinity} Pr(G_{n,cn;3} is Hamiltonian). Conjecture: L_c = 1 for all c >= 3/2. [Following slides: conjecture true for c = 3/2 (Robinson and Wormald 1984, the random cubic graph); Bollobas, Cooper, Fenner, Frieze (2000): L_c = 1 for c >= 128; Frieze (2012): L_c = 1 for c >= 10; 'Conjecture true for c >= 3, assuming numerical solution of some differential equations'. Here G_{n,m;3} is uniform over graphs with n vertices, m edges and minimum degree at least 3.]

title: Almost sure finiteness of avalanches for the stationary sandpile on Z^2
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Open Question 6.7. Consider Z^2. Is it true that for nu-a.e. eta the configuration eta + 1_0 can be stabilised with finitely many topplings? (Here nu is the infinite-volume weak limit of the stationary sandpile measures. The source notes E_nu[n(o,x)] = lim_n G_n(o,x) = infinity for all x: on average every vertex topples infinitely often. On transient graphs, under the one-end assumption, avalanches are finite by Theorem 6.6.)
source: Jarai: Sandpile models (Probab. Surveys 2018)
why_important: Finiteness of avalanches for the stationary sandpile on Z^2.
where_it_stands: Proved in high dimension; the planar case needs a recurrence argument.

title: Reconstruction is monotone in the number of Potts states at fixed second eigenvalue
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: Conjecture 4. Consider two symmetric channels M_1 and M_2 (as in (8)) on q_1 and q_2 symbols respectively, where q_1 < q_2. If 0 < lambda_2(M_1) = lambda_2(M_2) and the reconstruction problem is solvable for M_1, then it is also solvable for M_2. [Same page: 'This is obvious when q_2 is a multiple of q_1. Using the reconstruction criterion for the binary symmetric channel on 2 symbols, it is easy to prove the conjecture when q_1 = 2.' and 'it is easy to see that if the reconstruction problem is solvable for q and epsilon and q' < q, then the reconstruction problem is also solvable for q' and epsilon. We expect that for fixed lambda = lambda_2(M), reconstruction is easier when q is larger.'] [Setting of the source, Sections 2-4: T_b is the b-ary tree; a channel M is a q x q stochastic matrix (an ergodic Markov chain on the finite alphabet A); the root state is chosen, each vertex draws its state from its parent's through M independently; sigma_n is the configuration at level n; the reconstruction problem is solvable if the total variation distance between the laws of sigma_n given root i and given root j does not tend to 0 (Proposition 2.1: equivalently the mutual information I(sigma_rho, sigma_n) stays bounded away from 0); census-solvable if the same holds for the census c_n = (number of vertices at level n in each state); lambda_2(M) is the second largest eigenvalue of M in absolute value; Theorem 4.1: census-solvable if b|lambda_2(M)|^2 > 1 and not census-solvable if b|lambda_2(M)|^2 < 1. The symmetric q-state channel (8) is M_{i,i} = 1 - (q-1) epsilon, M_{i,j} = epsilon for i != j, with lambda_2(M) = 1 - q epsilon; ferromagnetic when lambda_2 > 0, antiferromagnetic when lambda_2 < 0; proper colourings are (9): M_{i,j} = 1{i != j}/(q-1).]
source: Mossel: Survey: Information flow on trees (2004)
why_important: Monotonicity of tree reconstruction in the number of Potts states.
where_it_stands: Reconstruction thresholds are known in many regimes.

title: Can the instability set in the jump rate be a union of several intervals?

Prove that the mean number of clusters per site kappa(p) = E_p(|C|^{-1}) behaves like |1/2 - p|^{2+alpha+o(1)}, where C is the cluster at the origin and alpha = -2/3.' Is there a delta > 0 such that P_{G_{n,d}}(Corr_{p_c(n)}(f_n(omega), f_n(omega^eps)) > delta) tends to 1 as n tends to infinity? The source notes that establishing this would require showing that the critical density theta(G) concentrates around its mean, for instance that P(theta(G) > 1 - 2 eps) tends to 1, and suggests trying Azuma-Hoeffding for a Lipschitz martingale exploring G_{n,d} edge by edge or in the configuration model.

domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability

title: Giant-component density from Erlang weighted-tree survival
domain_name: Random graphs and networks

title: Optimal exponent for the computational complexity of randomised algorithms for percolation crossings
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs

source: Garban and Steif: Noise sensitivity of Boolean functions and percolation, lecture notes with open problems

title: Noise sensitivity of simple random walk on Liouville Cayley graphs
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: [Verbatim from the source, Section 3.3.4.] Consider n steps simple random walk (SRW) X_n on a Cayley graph of a finitely generated infinite group Gamma. Refresh independently each step with probability epsilon, to get Y_n from X_n. Are there groups for which the positions at time n, X_n and Y_n are asymptotically independent? That is, the l_1 (total variation) distance between the chain (X_n, Y_n) and two independent copies (X'_n, X''_n) is going to 0, with n. Note that on the line Z, they are uniformally correlated, and therefore also on any group with a non trivial homomorphism to R, or any group that has a finite index subgroup with a non trivial homomorphism to R. On the free group and for any non-Liouville group, X_n and Y_n are correlated as well, but for a different reason: Both X_n and Y_n have nontrivial correlation with X_1. Itai Benjamini and Jeremie Brieussel conjecture that these are the only ways not to be noise sensitive. That is, if a Cayley graph is Liouville and the group does not have a finite index subgroup with a homomorphism to the reals, then the Cayley graph is noise sensitive for the simple random walk. In particular, the Grigorchuk group is noise sensitive for the simple random walk!
source: Kalai: Three puzzles on mathematics, computation, and games (ICM 2018)
locator: Section 3.3.4 (a problem of Benjamini and Brieussel), PDF p. 22
why_important: Noise sensitivity of random walk on Liouville groups.
where_it_stands: Entropy and boundary theory of groups give tools.

title: A Marstrand projection theorem for the zero set of the Brownian sheet
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE
