Theorem 1.1 of the source shows the projection of B^{-1}{0} onto the x-axis has the Marstrand property. Is there a RANDOM orthogonal projection whose image of B^{-1}{0} has Hausdorff dimension different from 2 - d/2? The source believes the answer is no but has neither proof nor counterexample.
source: Khoshnevisan: Slices of Brownian sheet, new results and open problems
why_important: Projection theorems for the zero set of the Brownian sheet.
where_it_stands: Projection results for related random sets are known.

title: Maximal integer superharmonic matrices in dimensions d >= 3

title: Convergence of height-fraction statistics in the sandpile scaling limit
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Refine the Pegden-Smart weak-* convergence of the rescaled sandpile s_n by showing that for any ball B and integer j the fraction of sites in B with exactly j particles converges as the lattice spacing tends to zero; also determine the scaling limit of the sandpile identity element.
source: Levine and Peres: Laplacian growth, sandpiles and scaling limits, BAMS 2017, with open problems

title: Sharpness of the Debye scale in Coulomb local laws
domain_name: Statistical mechanics: polymers, gases, interfaces
statement: Prove the conjectured sharpness of the temperature-dependent minimal Debye scale in the Coulomb local-energy laws, including the proposed Poissonian behavior below that scale.
statement_caveat: The source scale is rho_beta=C*max(1,sqrt(chi(beta)/beta)) in microscopic coordinates; chi(beta) is the source dimension-dependent correction. In d>=3 it is1. All temperature and dimension cases are one scale-sharpness question.
source: Serfaty: Lectures on Coulomb and Riesz gases,2024
why_important: Sharpness of the Debye scale for Coulomb gases.
where_it_stands: Local laws down to the Debye scale are proved.

title: Fluctuations of the heavy-tailed directed polymer at fixed temperature for tail exponent alpha > 5
domain_name: Statistical mechanics: polymers, gases, interfaces
statement: Context: the directed polymer in d = 1 with disorder in the domain of attraction of an alpha-stable law (Assumption 3, tail exponent alpha) and inverse temperature beta_n = hat-beta n^{-gamma}; the phase diagram in (alpha, gamma) is described by the source's Theorems 5.3-5.5 (energy-dominated stable fluctuations for 1/2 < alpha < 2 and gamma >= 3/(2 alpha), variational problems below that curve, a Gaussian regime for alpha in (2,6] and gamma >= 3/(2 alpha)). 'Question 5. Derive the limiting behaviours in the rest of the phase diagram. Do Airy and KPZ asymptotics extend when gamma = 0 and alpha > 5?'
source: Zygouras: Directed polymers in a random environment: a review of the phase transitions
why_important: Fluctuations of heavy-tailed directed polymers.
where_it_stands: Scaling limits are identified in neighbouring regimes.

title: Fuglede-Kadison product-measure bounds for equivariant determinantal processes
domain_name: Stationary processes and nonlinear Markov operators
statement: For every Gamma-equivariant positive contraction Q on l^2(Gamma), P_Q stochastically dominates the product measure with density FK(Q) = exp tr log|Q| and is dominated by the product measure with density 1 - FK(I-Q), and these bounds are optimal; open even for finite groups.
source: Lyons: Determinantal probability, basic properties and conjectures, ICM 2014
why_important: Lyons' conjecture that an equivariant determinantal process on a group lies, in the stochastic order, between the product measures of densities FK(Q) and 1 - FK(I - Q), FK the Fuglede-Kadison determinant, and that these bounds are optimal; it would extend the Lyons-Steif domination theorem from Z^d to every group.
where_it_stands: Proved for stationary determinantal processes on Z^d, with the bounds optimal (Lyons and Steif, 2003; Theorem 5.2 of the source). The source says the conjecture is open even for finite groups.

title: Invariant measures for full line TASEP with killing at one site
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Characterize invariant measures for unit-rate full-line TASEP with particles at site0 removed at a fixed positive rate kappa, as proposed in workshop systemS2.

source: AIM all roads to KPZ workshop follow-up report,2025
why_important: Invariant measures of TASEP with killing at one site.
where_it_stands: Explicit dynamics on the line.

title: Conjecture 1.4 (Sharp threshold for tree universality) of arXiv:2608.06358
domain_name: Random graphs and networks
statement: "For every ε>0 and integer Δ≥2, whp G(n,(1+ε)ln n/n) is 𝒯_{n,Δ}-universal."
locator: Conjecture 1.4 (Sharp threshold for tree universality); Section 1.6, "Further challenges"
why_important: Sharp threshold for spanning-tree universality of random graphs.
where_it_stands: Universality is known at a constant factor above the threshold.

title: Minimality of ergodic gradient Gibbs measures of finite free energy
domain_name: Statistical mechanics: polymers, gases, interfaces
statement: "[70, Conjecture 10.3.2] conjectures that if mu-nabla is ergodic and slope(mu-nabla) is in the interior of S then SFE(mu-nabla) < infinity", and Conjecture 10.3.1 "conjectures that if mu-nabla is ergodic, SFE(mu-nabla) < infinity and s = slope(mu-nabla) is in the interior of S then mu-nabla is minimal". The source notes these are proved for Lipschitz height functions or isotropic interactions, "We are not aware of results on which interactions V (if any) admit" the general case.
why_important: Finite specific free energy for ergodic gradient Gibbs measures.
where_it_stands: A conjecture of Sheffield with the relevant tools in the source.

title: Divergence of the 1/d expansion of the connective constant
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Prove that the asymptotic expansion of the connective constant mu(d) of Z^d in powers of 1/(2d) has radius of convergence zero (expected but unproved; coefficients known to order 11 grow rapidly).
source: Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman, Slade: Lectures on self-avoiding walks, Clay 2012
why_important: Divergence of the 1/d expansion of the self-avoiding walk connective constant.
where_it_stands: Many coefficients are known and grow factorially.

title: Analyticity of the one-dimensional Riesz free energy
domain_name: Statistical mechanics: polymers, gases, interfaces
statement: Prove the expected real analyticity in inverse temperature beta of the thermodynamic free energy of the one-dimensional long-range Riesz gas0<s<1 defined in the source.
statement_caveat: The source discusses deriving twice differentiability from its correlation and convergence results and expects full analyticity. Neither a possible C2 consequence nor convergence of periodic laws is counted as analyticity.
source: Boursier: Decay of correlations and thermodynamic limit for circular Riesz gas
why_important: Analyticity of the free energy of long-range Riesz gases.
where_it_stands: Decay of correlations is proved in the source.

title: DLR characterization of the circular Riesz thermodynamic limit
domain_name: Statistical mechanics: polymers, gases, interfaces
statement: Prove that the thermodynamic limit of the circular one-dimensional Riesz gas constructed in Boursier satisfies the anticipated infinite-volume DLR equations.
statement_caveat: The paper proves convergence of the finite circular laws for0<s<1 and s>1 and explicitly says the DLR characterization remains open. This is existence of the specification identity for that limit, distinct from uniqueness among all Gibbs states.
source: Boursier: Decay of correlations and thermodynamic limit for circular Riesz gas
why_important: DLR equations for the circular Riesz gas limit.
where_it_stands: The analogue for sine-beta is proved.

title: When does the support of the limiting measure equal the accumulation set of the branching random walk?
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: Give conditions under which the support of the limiting measure W coincides almost surely with the set of accumulation points of the branching random walk B on the boundary. The source notes that most of the existing literature on the boundary behaviour of branching random walk studies the accumulation set rather than the measure.
source: On the boundary at infinity for branching random walk
why_important: Support of the limit measure of branching random walk on hyperbolic boundaries.
where_it_stands: Explicit boundary theory for hyperbolic groups.

title: Tight subcritical bound on the largest component in terms of the maximum degree and the spectral radius
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Bernoulli bond percolation G_p on a finite graph G with maximum degree Delta(G) and spectral radius lambda(G), p <= (1 - eps)/lambda(G). Theorem 1.4 of the source: a.a.s. the largest component has size at most O( sqrt(|G| Delta(G)) log|G| / lambda(G) ), optimal when lambda(G) >> sqrt|G| (e.g. K_{s,s^3}) but not in all regimes (for lambda(G) = Delta(G) and G connected the true bound is O(log |G|)). Question 5.2. For a graph with given Delta(G) and lambda(G), what is the tight upper bound for the typical size of the largest component of G_p, when p <= (1 - eps)/lambda(G)? The source singles out the near-regular case Delta(G) <= (1 + delta) lambda(G).
source: Christoph, Morawski, Wigderson: The critical probability for percolation on finite graphs (2026)
why_important: Largest subcritical component of percolation on a finite graph.
where_it_stands: A bound in terms of maximum degree and spectral radius is proved.

title: Transience of the dual infinite Boltzmann map for a in [2, 5/2)
domain_name: Gaussian fields, LQG and planar maps
statement: Let q be a critical weight sequence of type a in [2, 5/2); is the dual map m-dagger of the infinite Boltzmann map of the plane transient for simple random walk under P^{(1)}_infinity?
source: Curien: Peeling random planar maps, Saint-Flour XLIX 2019 lecture notes, author preliminary version
why_important: Transience of the dual of infinite Boltzmann planar maps.
where_it_stands: Peeling exploration handles the neighbouring parameter range.

title: Filled-in peeling discovers the whole map for every critical weight sequence
domain_name: Gaussian fields, LQG and planar maps
statement: Corollary 27 shows that for a critical weight sequence of type a in [3/2, 5/2] a filled-in peeling exploration of the infinite Boltzmann map almost surely exhausts the map; is this true for every critical weight sequence?
source: Curien: Peeling random planar maps, Saint-Flour XLIX 2019 lecture notes, author preliminary version
why_important: Does filled-in peeling explore the whole map?
where_it_stands: Proved for part of the parameter range.

title: The thickness spectrum of a point on an LQG geodesic
domain_name: Gaussian fields, LQG and planar maps
statement: Let xi > 0 and let P be a D_h-geodesic for the LQG metric. Compute the Hausdorff dimension of the intersection of P with the set T^alpha_h of alpha-thick points, for each alpha in [-2,2], with respect to both D_h and the Euclidean metric. More weakly, is there a unique value of alpha maximising this dimension, i.e. a typical thickness for a point on an LQG geodesic? The analogue for the boundary of a metric ball is solved, with maximiser alpha = xi (Euclidean) and alpha = gamma (LQG).
source: Ding, Dubedat, Gwynne: Introduction to the Liouville quantum gravity metric
why_important: Thick points on Liouville quantum gravity geodesics.
where_it_stands: Dimension computations for related sets are done.

title: Crossover at drift 4/5 for the bad configurations of reduced random walk in random scenery
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Conjecture 2.16. Consider the random walk on Z with F = {-1, +1}, m_F(+1) = p and m_F(-1) = 1 - p, where p in [1/2, 1]. For p in [1/2, 4/5) every configuration (Y_n)_{n != 0} is bad for Y_0, while for p in (4/5, 1] every configuration (Y_n)_{n != 0} is good for Y_0. [Same page: 'We are presently attempting to prove this conjecture. If true, it would provide us with a remarkable example where the continuity problem has a phase transition in the drift parameter.' The scenery here is the two-colour i.i.d. scenery of Section 2.6, values in {-1, +1}.] [Setting of the source, Section 1 and Section 2.6: X = (X_n)_{n in Z} i.i.d. Z^d-valued increments with law m_F (F the set of possible values), S the random walk S_n = X_1 + ... + X_n (S_0 = 0, S_{-n} = -(X_0 + ... + X_{-n+1})), C = (C_z)_{z in Z^d} an i.i.d. scenery with law m_G on a finite set G, independent of X; Y_n = C_{S_n} the scenery seen along the walk; RWRS is the joint process Z_n = (X_n, Y_n) and 'reduced RWRS' is (Y_n) alone. PDF p. 8: Lambda_n = [-n, n] cap Z; a configuration (W_n)_{n != 0} is a bad configuration for W_0 if there is an epsilon > 0 such that for all n in N there are m >= n and a configuration zeta agreeing with W on Lambda_n minus {0} such that the two conditional laws of W_0 given the configurations on Lambda_m minus {0} differ by at least epsilon in total variation; a configuration that is not bad is called good; every version of the conditional probability is discontinuous at the bad configurations and there is a version continuous at all good ones (Maes, Redig, Van Moffaert).]
source: den Hollander, Steif: Random walk in random scenery: a survey of some recent results (2006)
why_important: A crossover in random walk in random scenery.
where_it_stands: An explicit one-dimensional model.

title: Best edge to add to a regular graph to speed up the random walk
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: One may ask the analogue of Question 3 for random walk on any graph: for a connected d-regular graph on an even number n of vertices, which edge (or perfect matching) should be added to best speed up the nearest-neighbour random walk?
source: Diaconis: Some things we have learned (about Markov chain Monte Carlo)
why_important: Which edge speeds up random walk on a regular graph the most?
where_it_stands: Spectral perturbation on a finite graph.

title: Typical mixing rate of a random random walk on a general finite group
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For an arbitrary finite group G, if a generating set S is chosen at random, what is the typical rate of convergence of the random walk it generates? The source notes that this is the topic of random random walks, surveyed by Hildebrand, and that the best bounds on the diameter of random Cayley graphs are due to Babai, Beals and Seress, which can be turned into mixing bounds.
source: Diaconis: Some things we have learned (about Markov chain Monte Carlo)
why_important: Mixing of random walk with random generators on a general group.
where_it_stands: Known for abelian and some other groups.

title: The extremal ray-height constant in a heavy-tailed branching random walk
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: Identify the positive finite constant a1 in inf_ray limsup_n V(ray_n)/sqrt(n*log n)=a1 under Theorem1.2.
statement_caveat: This is the value of the source constant, not the already established existence theorem. Its full tilted-tail and logarithmic moment assumptions are retained by reference.
source: Aidekon-Hu-Shi: Boundedness of discounted tree sums
why_important: The extremal ray constant in branching random walk.
where_it_stands: The order is proved; the constant is the target.

title: Weak convergence of the disordered zero-range process from a spatially ergodic start
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Fix the site rates alpha and take the initial distribution of eta(0) spatially ergodic with density rho. Does the law of eta(t) converge weakly as t tends to infinity to one of the equilibria nu^alpha_phi? If rho > rho* in the phase-transition case, does eta(t) converge weakly to the equilibrium with density rho*? The analogous statement for the standard (non-disordered) zero-range process is due to Andjel, Ferrari, Guiol and Landim type results.
source: Recent results and open problems on the hydrodynamics of disordered asymmetric exclusion and zero-range processes
why_important: Long-time behaviour of the disordered zero-range process.
where_it_stands: Hydrodynamic and condensation results exist.

title: Largest completely covered disc for a random walk in an annular region
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Consider D_n intersect H with D_n contained in the complement of the disc D(0, a_n), where a_n tends to infinity. What is the almost sure asymptotic of M_{D_n}(n), the maximal local time over that region? The source is especially interested in the case D_n contained in D(0,2 a_n) minus D(0, a_n) with a_n = n^alpha for 0 < alpha < 1/2, noting that the largest disc completely covered by the planar walk before time tau_n has radius n^{1/2 + o(1)}, and conjectures that for a_n at least n^{1/2 + eps} a corresponding statement holds.
source: Topics and problems on favorite sites of random walks
why_important: Covered discs for planar random walk in an annulus.
where_it_stands: Cover-time machinery for the planar walk is developed.

title: Vanishing drift for conjugation-invariant metrics on symmetric measured groups
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Let (G, mu) be a symmetric measured group and suppose there exists a bi-invariant (conjugation-invariant) and mu-integrable (semi-)metric d on G. Is the drift delta_d(mu) equal to 0? The source suggests as a first test case the commutator subgroup of the free group on two generators with the stable commutator length.
source: Five remarks about random walks on groups
why_important: Drift of random walks for conjugation-invariant metrics.
where_it_stands: A boundary-theory question for symmetric measures.

title: Continuity of the uniqueness threshold in the retention parameter: is N(p) monotone in p on transitive graphs?
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: For i.i.d. bond percolation on a transitive graph, show that the number of infinite clusters N(p) cannot switch back and forth between infinity and 1 as p increases: the set of p with uniqueness is an interval [p_u, 1] (proved for transitive graphs by Haggstrom-Peres and Schonmann; the survey records the general question for quasi-transitive and for non-unimodular graphs as settled only in the transitive case).
source: Haggstrom and Jonasson: Uniqueness and non-uniqueness in percolation theory, Probability Surveys 2006, with open problems
why_important: Monotonicity of the number of infinite percolation clusters.
where_it_stands: Uniqueness monotonicity is known; the question excludes back-and-forth switching.

title: Cluster repulsion for nonunimodular transitive graphs
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Does every transitive graph exhibit cluster repulsion, i.e. two distinct infinite clusters at level p almost surely do not come within bounded distance of each other along an infinite set of sites (Haggstrom-Peres-Schonmann conjecture)? Timar proved it for unimodular transitive graphs by mass transport; the nonunimodular case is open.
source: Haggstrom and Jonasson: Uniqueness and non-uniqueness in percolation theory, Probability Surveys 2006, with open problems
why_important: Cluster repulsion on transitive graphs.
where_it_stands: Proved for unimodular transitive graphs (Timar, 2006). For nonunimodular quasi-transitive graphs, Bell, Chu, Rodgers, Terlov and Tserunyan (arXiv:2509.10631, 2025) proved that for any two heavy clusters the vertices of one within distance one of the other form a set of finite total weight; light clusters, and finiteness in place of finite weight, remain open.

title: Tail of the allocation distance for the critical stable marriage of Poisson and Lebesgue
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Open problems (ii) Critical tail behavior. What is the tail behavior of X for the critical Poisson model? In particular, give any quantitative upper bound for d >= 2. [Setting: centres form a Poisson process of intensity 1 in R^d with appetite alpha = 1 (critical: total appetite equals volume), X is the distance from a typical site to its centre; the source proves E X^d = infinity in the critical case (Theorem 32 for the site-to-centre distance under insertion tolerance) and power-law lower bounds, and says in its abstract 'It is an open problem to prove any upper bound in d > 1'.]
source: Hoffman, Holroyd, Peres: A stable marriage of Poisson and Lebesgue (Ann. Probab. 2006)
locator: Open problems (ii) Critical tail behavior, Section 12, PDF p. 31
why_important: Tail of the stable marriage of Poisson and Lebesgue at criticality.
where_it_stands: Subcritical and supercritical tails are known.

title: Percolation of claimed and unclaimed sites in the stable marriage of Poisson and Lebesgue
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Open problems (iii) Percolation. In the Poisson model, does the set of unclaimed sites have an infinite component for alpha sufficiently small? Does it fail to have an infinite component for sufficiently large alpha < 1? Similar questions apply to the set of claimed sites. After this paper was accepted for publication, progress on these problems was achieved in [5]. [[5] is Freire, Popov and Vachkovskaia, 'Percolation for the stable marriage of Poisson and Lebesgue', Stoch. Proc. Appl. 2007. Setting: centres form a Poisson process of intensity 1 in R^d, appetite alpha < 1, so a positive fraction 1 - alpha of the volume is unclaimed.]
source: Hoffman, Holroyd, Peres: A stable marriage of Poisson and Lebesgue (Ann. Probab. 2006)
locator: Open problems (iii) Percolation, Section 12, PDF p. 31
why_important: Percolation of claimed and unclaimed sites in stable marriage.
where_it_stands: Explicit translation-invariant construction.

title: Convergence to equilibrium for FA-1f from any initial law with an infection
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: For the Fredrickson-Andersen one-spin facilitated model on Z with infection density q in (0,1): for any q and any local function f, E_nu(f(eta(t))) tends to pi(f) as t tends to infinity, provided nu(there exists an infected vertex) = 1. Here pi is the Bernoulli(q) product measure, which is reversible for the dynamics.
source: Long time behaviour of one facilitated kinetically constrained models: results and open problems
why_important: Convergence to equilibrium for the FA-1f kinetically constrained model.
where_it_stands: Proved for special initial laws.

title: Exponential relaxation of FA-1f from an initial law with exponentially rare infection gaps
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: For FA-1f on Z: if there is kappa > 0 with nu(no infected vertices in [-l, l]) = O(exp(-kappa l)) for all large l, then for every q > 0 the convergence of E_nu(f(eta(t))) to pi(f) is exponentially fast.
source: Long time behaviour of one facilitated kinetically constrained models: results and open problems
why_important: Exponential relaxation of FA-1f under rare infection gaps.
where_it_stands: Proved for special initial laws.

title: One-dimensional boundary two-star set in LQG
domain_name: Gaussian fields, LQG and planar maps
statement: For the gamma-LQG metric associated with a Neumann GFF on the upper half plane, is the metric Hausdorff dimension of the boundary two-star set exactly1?
statement_caveat: The boundary intersection uses the ambient LQG metric restricted to the boundary, not an intrinsic boundary path metric. The established lower bound1 is not the requested equality.
source: Bhatia Gwynne Harper: Dimension lower bounds in random geometry via Lipschitz functions (2026)
why_important: Dimension of the boundary two-star set in LQG.
where_it_stands: Bulk analogues are computed.

title: Survival probability of the critical Derrida-Retaux recursion decays like 4/((m-1)^2 n^2)
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: Assume the critical condition (m-1) E(X_0 m^{X_0}) = E(m^{X_0}) < infinity with X_0 valued in Z_+. Then P(X_n != 0) is asymptotic to (4/(m-1)^2) n^{-2} as n tends to infinity. For m = 2 this was already conjectured by Collet et al. and by Derrida and Retaux.
source: A max-type recursive model: some properties and open questions
why_important: Survival asymptotics of the critical Derrida-Retaux recursion.
where_it_stands: The order of decay is known in special cases.

title: Diffusion limit for an arbitrary symmetric M/G/1 discipline
domain_name: Queueing and stochastic networks
statement: For every work-conserving symmetric discipline gamma, prove convergence of Q_gamma(r^2 t)/r to the common reflected Brownian limit when the service second moment is finite and r(1-rho_r) tends to beta.
statement_caveat: Use empty initial state, as in the source discussion of universal marginal laws. PS and LCFS are known special cases, not new solutions.
source: Zwart: Conjectures on Symmetric Queues in Heavy Traffic
why_important: Diffusion limits for symmetric queueing disciplines.
where_it_stands: Known for several disciplines; the claim is a universal limit.

title: Classification of the solutions of the star-scale-invariance equation
domain_name: Gaussian fields, LQG and planar maps
statement: Classify the solutions M of the star-equation (star-scale invariance) according to the parameters alpha and gamma: (1) if alpha = 1 and gamma^2 < 2d, M is the standard Gaussian multiplicative chaos; (2) if alpha = 1 and gamma^2 = 2d, M is the derivative martingale M'; (3) if alpha < 1 and gamma^2 < 2d, M is an atomic chaos of the dual phase; (4) if alpha < 1 and gamma^2 = 2d, M is an atomic chaos of the frozen phase.
source: Rhodes and Vargas: Gaussian multiplicative chaos and applications, a review
locator: Conjecture 6.4 (Solutions to the star-equation), Section 6.3, PDF p. 52
why_important: Classification of star-scale invariant random measures.
where_it_stands: Log-normal solutions are classified.

title: Sharpness of kappa <= 1 for non-ballisticity of the Dirichlet walk in dimension two
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: As we will see below (Theorem 5), the assumption kappa <= 1 is sharp in dimension d >= 3, and this is also conjectured to be true in dimension 2. [I.e. the conjecture: for the RWDE on Z^2 with d_alpha != 0 and kappa > 1, lim X_n/n = v exists and is non-zero, P_0^(alpha)-a.s. Context, PDF p. 17, Remark 7: 'A famous conjecture is that for uniformly elliptic RWRE in dimension d >= 2, directional transience implies ballisticity. We see that it is not true for non uniformly elliptic environment, in particular for Dirichlet environment. Nevertheless, the previous theorem shows that with a slightly different notion of ballisticity, which involves the parameter kappa which is a function of the environment, directional transience implies ballisticity. It hence gives in dimension d >= 3 for Dirichlet environments an answer to the conjecture. It is expected that the same is true in dimension d = 2, but we are still far for a proof of that.'] [Setting of the source, Sections 2-5: a random walk in Dirichlet environment (RWDE) on Z^d with weights alpha_1, ..., alpha_{2d} > 0 attached to the 2d nearest-neighbour directions e_1, ..., e_{2d} (e_{i+d} = -e_i): at each site the transition probabilities (omega(x, x + e_i))_i are an independent Dirichlet(alpha_1, ..., alpha_{2d}) vector; P^(alpha) is the law of the environment, P_0^(alpha) the annealed law of the walk from 0. d_alpha := sum_{i=1}^{2d} alpha_i e_i is the mean drift direction; kappa := 2 sum_{i=1}^{2d} alpha_i - max_{1 <= i <= d} (alpha_i + alpha_{i+d}) (PDF p. 11, (4.3)) is the integrability exponent of the Green function of the strongest finite trap (a pair of neighbours). Theorem 1 (PDF p. 12): if d_alpha . l != 0 the walk is transient in the direction of sign(d_alpha . l) l, and if d_alpha != 0 it has asymptotic direction d_alpha/|d_alpha|, P_0^(alpha)-a.s. Proposition 2 (PDF p. 11): if kappa <= 1 then X_n/n -> 0. Theorem 5 (PDF p. 16): (i) if d >= 3, d_alpha != 0 and kappa > 1 then X_n/n -> v != 0; (ii) if d_alpha = 0 or kappa <= 1 then X_n/n -> 0; (iii) if d >= 3, d_alpha . l > 0 and kappa <= 1 then log(X_n . l)/log n -> kappa in probability. (T)^gamma is Sznitman's ballisticity condition (exponential decay, at rate L^gamma, of the annealed probability of exiting a slab of width L on the wrong side).]
source: Sabot, Tournier: Random walks in Dirichlet environment: an overview (2016)
locator: Section 4, PDF p. 11 (the sentence following Proposition 2)
why_important: Ballisticity threshold for random walk in Dirichlet environment in the plane.
where_it_stands: Sharp in dimension at least three.

title: Sznitman's condition (T)^gamma holds for every directionally transient Dirichlet walk
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: It is expected that this condition is not optimal, and we conjecture that at least (T)^gamma is satisfied when d_alpha != 0, hence that renewal times have finite s-moments for s < kappa when the RWDE is directionally transient, i.e. when d_alpha != 0. [Context, PDF pp. 18-19: Corollary 2: 'Assume that d >= 2 and that d_alpha . l > 0 for some direction l. Assume that the condition (6.1) is satisfied, and denote (tau_k)_{k >= 1} the renewal times in the direction l. Then E_0[tau_1^s] < infinity if and only if s < kappa.' Condition (6.1) is the source's sufficient condition for (T)^gamma (a lower bound on the weights in a half space, from Bouchet-Ramirez-Sabot and Fribergh-Kious); 'this condition' in the conjecture is (6.1).] [Setting of the source, Sections 2-5: a random walk in Dirichlet environment (RWDE) on Z^d with weights alpha_1, ..., alpha_{2d} > 0 attached to the 2d nearest-neighbour directions e_1, ..., e_{2d} (e_{i+d} = -e_i): at each site the transition probabilities (omega(x, x + e_i))_i are an independent Dirichlet(alpha_1, ..., alpha_{2d}) vector; P^(alpha) is the law of the environment, P_0^(alpha) the annealed law of the walk from 0. d_alpha := sum_{i=1}^{2d} alpha_i e_i is the mean drift direction; kappa := 2 sum_{i=1}^{2d} alpha_i - max_{1 <= i <= d} (alpha_i + alpha_{i+d}) (PDF p. 11, (4.3)) is the integrability exponent of the Green function of the strongest finite trap (a pair of neighbours). Theorem 1 (PDF p. 12): if d_alpha . l != 0 the walk is transient in the direction of sign(d_alpha . l) l, and if d_alpha != 0 it has asymptotic direction d_alpha/|d_alpha|, P_0^(alpha)-a.s. Proposition 2 (PDF p. 11): if kappa <= 1 then X_n/n -> 0. Theorem 5 (PDF p. 16): (i) if d >= 3, d_alpha != 0 and kappa > 1 then X_n/n -> v != 0; (ii) if d_alpha = 0 or kappa <= 1 then X_n/n -> 0; (iii) if d >= 3, d_alpha . l > 0 and kappa <= 1 then log(X_n . l)/log n -> kappa in probability. (T)^gamma is Sznitman's ballisticity condition (exponential decay, at rate L^gamma, of the annealed probability of exiting a slab of width L on the wrong side).]
source: Sabot, Tournier: Random walks in Dirichlet environment: an overview (2016)
locator: Section 6.1, PDF p. 19 (the sentence following Corollary 2)
why_important: Sznitman's ballisticity condition for Dirichlet environments.
where_it_stands: Proved under a stronger condition.

title: Endogeny of nonminimal discounted-tree fixed points
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: Determine whether every positive-index invariant RTP from Corollary33 and condition39 is nonendogenous.
statement_caveat: The counterexample is restricted to literal zero-mark/unit-weight boundary assumptions. The intended strictly discounted nondegenerate regime remains unsolved.
source: Aldous and Bandyopadhyay: A survey of max-type recursive distributional equations
why_important: Endogeny of recursive tree processes.
where_it_stands: A partial result is recorded in the problem's ledger row.

title: Limit constant for common random two-dimensional partial orders
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: Prove that the mean size of the largest common induced suborder of two independent uniform two-dimensional partial orders is asymptotic to c*n^(1/3), and determine c.
statement_caveat: The source already gives order n^(1/3) upper and lower arguments. The calculation here makes a constant in its grid lower construction explicit; it is a rederivation of an established method, not resolution of the limit question.
source: Aldous open problems: Largest common random substructures
why_important: Common substructures of random partial orders.
where_it_stands: Subadditivity gives the exponent; the constant is the target.

title: The four-dimensional case of the closer-to-a-car question
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: The source answers the analogue of Open Question 3 ("P(the origin is closer to a free spot than to a driving car at time t) -> 0 ?") "affirmatively when d <= 3" and "construct[s] counterexamples when d >= 5". The case d = 4 is left open by that pair of results.
locator: Theorem 1.5 and the discussion of Damron, Gravner, Junge, Lyu and Sivakoff [2019, Open Question 3]
why_important: The four-dimensional case of a parking question.
where_it_stands: Dimensions up to three are answered in the source.

title: A uniform strict improvement of the spectral gap constant for noncubic degrees
domain_name: Random graphs and networks
statement: "A uniform strict improvement for noncubic graphs implies that, for every sufficiently large even order, the maximum is attained uniquely by the cubic graph of least algebraic connectivity." The source proves that every noncubic degree admits a uniformly larger spectral-gap constant but leaves the uniform strict improvement that would give uniqueness of the extremiser.
why_important: Extremal spectral gap among graphs of a given order.
where_it_stands: The cubic case is proved in the source.

title: Almost-sure convergence in the heavy-tailed circular law
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Upgrade the convergence in probability of the empirical spectral distribution of n^{-1/alpha} X (i.i.d. entries in the domain of attraction of an alpha-stable law, alpha in (0,2)) to almost-sure weak convergence to mu_alpha.
source: Bordenave and Chafai: Around the circular law, survey with open problems
why_important: Almost sure convergence in the heavy-tailed circular law.
where_it_stands: Convergence in probability is proved.

title: Least singular values at the polynomial constant term
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Extend the polynomial least-singular-value bound for a nonzero holomorphic polynomial of independent complex Ginibre matrices to the shift equal to its constant term.
statement_caveat: The source theorem excludes that single shift. Qualitative invertibility and a quantitative polynomial lower-tail estimate are kept distinct.
source: Yi Han: Brown measure convergence for the spectrum of polynomials in Ginibre matrices
why_important: Least singular values of polynomials in Ginibre matrices.
where_it_stands: Proved away from the constant term.

title: Weak and strong disorder critical temperatures for directed Brownian polymers in a Poissonian environment
domain_name: Statistical mechanics: polymers, gases, interfaces
statement: For the directed Brownian polymer in a Poissonian environment, define the critical inverse temperatures beta_c^{+,dir} = sup{beta >= 0 : lim_t P[(W_t^{dir,beta})^{1/2}] > 0} and beta_c^{-,dir} = inf{beta >= 0 : lim_t P[(W_t^{dir,beta})^{1/2}] > 0}, the analogues of the weak/strong disorder transition. The survey formulates conjectures about these critical points for the directed model.
source: Brownian polymers in Poissonian environment: a survey
why_important: Critical temperatures of directed Brownian polymers in Poisson environments.
where_it_stands: Weak and strong disorder are characterised separately.

title: Stretched-exponential finite-cluster tail wherever theta(p) > 0 (site percolation, d >= 3)
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Bernoulli site percolation on Z^d, d >= 3, C(0) the cluster of the origin. Conjecture 1.4. Let d >= 3. For any p in ]0,1[, we have the implication theta(p, Z^d) > 0 => liminf_{n -> infinity} (1/ln n) ln ln (1 / P_p(n <= |C(0)| < +infinity)) > 0. [Context: Theorem 1.2 of the source proves that at p = p_c either theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0 or that liminf is 0; the source says 'it could be that the correct way to prove that theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0 is to prove separately theorem 1.3 and conjecture 1.4'.]
source: Cerf: theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0? (2026, 708 pp.)
why_important: Finite-cluster tails throughout the supercritical regime of site percolation.
where_it_stands: Known for bond percolation via slab arguments.

title: Second-order pivotal maximisers of increasing sets sit between Hamming levels n/2 - 2 and n/2 + 1
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: Setting of the source's Part on pivots (Sections 47-58): for an increasing subset A of {0,1}^n, P^+_k(A, omega) is the set of pivots of order k of A at omega and phi_2(A) = sum_omega |P^+_2(A, omega)|, phi_{2 \ 1}(A) the analogous sum over second-order pivots that are not first-order pivots (formulas (51.1) and (52.1) of the source). Conjecture 53.1. Let n >= 1 be fixed. If A* is an increasing subset of {0,1}^n which realizes the maximum of phi_{2\1} or of phi_2, then { omega : sum_i omega(i) >= n/2 + 1 } is contained in A* which is contained in { omega : sum_i omega(i) >= n/2 - 2 }. [The source: the conjecture 'holds for n <= 7' by exhaustive search and 'yields a valuable upper bound' E|P^+_2(A)| <= 6 sqrt(n) for every increasing A; Section 59 tries Steiner symmetrisation and fails.]
source: Cerf: theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0? (2026, 708 pp.)
why_important: Pivotal sets of increasing events.
where_it_stands: A combinatorial extremal question on the cube.

title: Forrester-Haldane pointwise pair-correlation asymptotics for sine beta
domain_name: Statistical mechanics: polymers, gases, interfaces
statement: Prove the predicted oscillatory large-distance expansion of the sine-beta truncated two-point correlation function for general beta, beyond the established special values and weaker averaged decay estimates.
statement_caveat: All harmonics and beta regimes are one asymptotic family. Lewin uses unit density; Dumaz-Malvy use density1/(2*pi), so distances must be rescaled before comparing coefficients.
source: Dumaz and Malvy: Long-Range Correlation of Sine beta Point Process (2026)
why_important: Correlation asymptotics for sine-beta point processes.
where_it_stands: Proved for special values of beta.

title: Is lambda_1 < lambda_p for the contact process on Z^d, d >= 2 (percolation of the upper invariant measure)
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Contact process with infection rate lambda on Z^d; lambda_1 the critical value for survival (lambda_1 = lambda_c on Z^d), and lambda_p the critical value beyond which the infected vertices of the upper invariant measure nu_lambda percolate. Source: '[8] proves in particular that ... lambda_p(Z) = +infinity, lambda_p(Z^d) <= 6.25 < +infinity for d >= 2. The same paper also raises the natural question whether we have lambda_1 < lambda_p on Z^d when d >= 2, which remains a difficult open problem. To the best of our knowledge, such a result has previously never been proven for any graph with lambda_p < +infinity.' The source proves lambda_1 < lambda_p on the regular tree T_d for all d >= 3 (and 0 < lambda_1 < lambda_p < lambda_2 < lambda_p^c < infinity for d >= 7).
source: Fernley, Jacob: Percolation of the contact process on the regular tree (2026)
why_important: Percolation of the upper invariant measure of the contact process.
where_it_stands: Comparison arguments with oriented percolation.

title: Continuity of the two percolation transitions of the upper invariant measure on T_d
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Contact process on the regular tree T_d with upper invariant measure nu_lambda; lambda_p the percolation threshold of the infected set, lambda_p^c the threshold before which the healthy set percolates. Source: 'the figure suggests that both transitions are continuous, and it's possible as well that the probability to be in an infinite healthy component has a continuous derivative at lambda = lambda_p^c while the probability to be in an infinite infected component at lambda = lambda_p does not. We leave both questions as interesting open problems.' Question: are the functions lambda -> nu_lambda(0 in an infinite infected component) and lambda -> nu_lambda(0 in an infinite healthy component) continuous at lambda_p and lambda_p^c respectively, and is the first derivative continuous at lambda_p^c but not at lambda_p?
source: Fernley, Jacob: Percolation of the contact process on the regular tree (2026)
why_important: Continuity of percolation thresholds for the contact process on trees.
where_it_stands: Explicit tree structure.

title: Increasing-events boundary-connectivity conjecture on finite graphs (implies theta(p_c) = 0)
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Bernoulli bond percolation with parameter p on a finite graph G = (V,E), o in V, B a subset of V. An event A is increasing with respect to the percolation configuration if omega -> P[A | pi = omega] is increasing on {0,1}^E (pi the configuration; the event may depend on extra randomness). Conjecture 2.2. There exists a universal function phi : (0, +infinity) -> R, independent of G, o, B and p, such that phi(eps) -> 1 as eps -> 0, and such that the following statement always holds. Let eps > 0. Let (E_b)_{b in B} be a family of events which are increasing with respect to the percolation configuration. Assume that P[E_b] >= 1 - eps for every b in B. Then P[ union_{b in B} ({o <-> b} cap E_b) ] >= phi(eps) P[o <-> B]. [Theorem 2.4 of the source: the conjecture implies theta(p_c) = 0 for every d >= 2, via Kozma and Nitzan's Theorem 6.]
source: Flammant: A finite-graph conjecture related to theta(p_c)=0 for Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^d (2026)
why_important: Boundary connectivity for increasing events on finite graphs.
where_it_stands: A finite-graph inequality with special cases proved.

title: Symmetric unimodality under free addition
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Is the free additive convolution of two symmetric unimodal probability laws unimodal?
statement_caveat: The older AIM free-analysis question is the same family and is not counted again. A semicircle factor and some freely infinitely divisible subclasses are established cases.
source: Hasebe-Ueda: Large time unimodality, published version
why_important: Unimodality of free convolutions of symmetric unimodal laws.
where_it_stands: Related unimodality questions for free Brownian motion are settled.

title: Location of Brownian modes at large time
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE
statement: Estimate the mode of classical Brownian motion started from a law with a finite exponential quadratic moment, and determine analogous estimates for free Brownian motion.
statement_caveat: The source gives a growing interval of radius sqrt(t)/2 once unimodality holds. Classical and free versions of this mode-location request are grouped.
source: Hasebe-Ueda: Large time unimodality, published version
why_important: The mode of Brownian motion and free Brownian motion at large time.
where_it_stands: Explicit heat-kernel and subordination formulas.

title: Does frozen-percolation endogeny imply unrestricted almost sure uniqueness?
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: When the burning-time RTP is endogenous, must all solutions to the frozen-percolation equation driven by the same innovations agree, even without stationarity, adaptation or subtree independence?
statement_caveat: Includes the source conjecture for geometric freezing sets theta<1/2; these are not counted as separate parameter questions.
source: Rath-Swart-Szoke: A phase transition between endogeny and nonendogeny
why_important: Uniqueness of frozen-percolation solutions under endogeny.
where_it_stands: Endogeny is known in the relevant regime.

title: Is the sandpile aggregate on a background of holes a regular (4H+12)-gon?
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Question 6.2. In Z^2, is the limiting shape of S_{n,H} as n -> infinity a regular (4H+12)-gon? [Same page: 'Simulations indicate that for general H >= -2, the limiting shape of S_{n,H} in Z^2 may be a polygon with 4H + 12 sides.' 'Simulations indicate a regular (4H + 12)-gon with some rounding at the corners; it remains unclear if the rounded portions of the boundary become negligible in the limit. Even if the limiting shape is not a polygon, it would still be very interesting to establish the weaker statement that it has the dihedral symmetry D_{4H+12}.' Figure 11: square, octagon and dodecagon for H = -2, -1, 0.] [Setting, Section 6, PDF p. 29: 'Fey-den Boer and Redig [FR07] consider aggregation in the sandpile model on Z^d. In their setup, the underlying graph for the chip-firing game is the infinite undirected d-dimensional cubic lattice Z^d. Start with each site containing h <= 2d - 2 chips. Here h may be even be taken negative, corresponding to starting with a hole of depth H = -h at each lattice site; that is, each site absorbs the first H chips it receives, and thereafter fires every time it receives an additional four chips. Now add n chips to the origin and stabilize. Denote by S_{n,H} the set of sites in Z^d which fired in the process of stabilization.' Theorem 6.1 ([FR07]): S_{n,2-2d} is a cube C(r_n) for every n; in Z^2, S_{n,-2} is a square. PDF p. 30: 'even the existence of a limiting shape for S_{n,H} has not been proved in the case H > -2', and as H -> infinity the limiting shape is a ball (Fey-Redig; Theorem 6.3 of Levine-Peres).]
source: Holroyd, Levine, Meszaros, Peres, Propp, Wilson: Chip-firing and rotor-routing on directed graphs (2008)
why_important: Limit shape of the sandpile with holes.
where_it_stands: Simulations are strong and divisible-sandpile methods exist.

title: Tail exponent of the two-colour stable Poisson matching in dimensions at least two
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Open Problems (i). For the two-color stable matching of two independent Poisson processes, what is the correct power law for the tail behavior of X in dimensions d >= 2? We conjecture that E* X^alpha < infinity if and only if alpha < d/2. [Setting: red and blue points are independent Poisson processes of intensity 1 in R^d; the two-colour stable matching is the Gale-Shapley matching obtained by iteratively matching mutually closest red-blue pairs; X is the distance from a typical (Palm) point to its partner and E* the Palm expectation. The source proves a power-law upper bound on P*(X > r) for this scheme, a power-law lower bound in all dimensions, and the exact tail in d = 1; for arbitrary translation-invariant two-colour schemes E* X^{d/2} = infinity in d = 1, 2 while schemes with finite exponential moments exist in d >= 3.]
source: Holroyd, Pemantle, Peres, Schramm: Poisson matching (Ann. IHP 2009)
why_important: Tail exponent for two-colour stable Poisson matching.
where_it_stands: One-colour and one-dimensional cases are known.

title: Non-crossing translation-invariant matching of two Poisson processes in the plane
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Open Problems (ii). Does there exist a translation-invariant matching of two independent Poisson processes in R^2 such that the line segments connecting matched pairs do not cross? [Two-colour setting as in the source: red and blue independent Poisson processes of intensity 1 in R^2, a perfect bipartite matching whose joint law with the points is translation-invariant.]
source: Holroyd, Pemantle, Peres, Schramm: Poisson matching (Ann. IHP 2009)
why_important: Non-crossing invariant matching of two Poisson processes.
where_it_stands: A construction question in the plane.

title: Scaling limit of the electric field exp(i alpha h) of the dimer height function
domain_name: Gaussian fields, LQG and planar maps
statement: 1. Height mod k. What can be said about the random variable e^{i alpha h} where alpha is a constant and h is the height function? This is an analog of the spin-spin correlations in the Ising model and is a more delicate quantity to measure than the height function itself. Standard Toeplitz techniques allow one to evaluate it in lattice directions, and it is conjectured to be rotationally invariant (for the uniform square grid dimers, say). See [24] for some partial results. Can one describe the scaling limit of this field? [Setting: uniform dimer model (domino tilings) on the square grid, h the height function.]
source: Kenyon: Lectures on dimers
locator: Open problems, item 1 (Height mod k), Section 12, PDF p. 54
why_important: Scaling limit of the electric correlator of dimers.
where_it_stands: The height function converges to the Gaussian free field.

title: Bramson correction for the front of threshold cascades on unimodular random trees
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees, in the setting of the source's Theorem 2.1 (supercritical branching-random-walk representation with tilt parameter theta*, speed c*, derivative martingale dW_n). Conjecture 3.2 (Uniform integrability of the derivative martingale => Bramson delay). Under the hypotheses of Theorem 2.1, the derivative martingale dW_n is uniformly integrable (equivalently, dW_infinity > 0 a.s. on survival), and consequently the time-indexed front obeys F(t) = c* t - (3/(2 theta* c*)) log t + O_P(1), with the tightness and the limiting law of the recentred front given by a randomly-shifted Gumbel decorated point process, the shift being a multiple of log dW_infinity, exactly as for branching Brownian motion. [Source's Programme 3.3 lists the three ingredients, of which the x log^2 x moment condition for the offspring point process is the missing one.]
source: Kumar, Dudeja: Two problems for threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees (2026)
why_important: Bramson correction for threshold cascades on trees.
where_it_stands: Branching random walk representation is proved.

title: Gaussian lower bound for noise stability of unbiased thresholds
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: For an unbiased linear threshold f and rho in(0,1), prove Stab_rho(f)>=(2/pi)*arcsin(rho).
statement_caveat: This is the authors refined conjecture, not the false finite-majority comparison. The degree-one Fourier lower bound2/pi and small-noise consequence are grouped as parts of this family.
source: Kamath,Kumar,Manurangsi: When Majority Fails,2026
locator: Section1.4, Conjecture1; O-Donnell2012 p.5 weaker consequences
why_important: A lower bound for the noise stability of unbiased thresholds.
where_it_stands: The Gaussian limit gives the conjectured constant.

title: Coverage asymptotics for the inertial Boolean model
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: For the mobile Boolean model, study the coverage problem, i.e. the law of inf{t >= 0 : K contained in W(t)}, the first time a compact set K is entirely covered by the moving grains. For the Brownian Boolean model, and as the diameter of the region tends to infinity, the problem has been solved; what are the corresponding asymptotics for the INERTIAL cases, in which the grains move ballistically with random velocities?
source: The mobile Boolean model: an overview and further results
why_important: Coverage time for moving random sets.
where_it_stands: Static coverage asymptotics are classical.

title: Rate of convergence in the circular law as a function of the moment assumption
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Determine the optimal rate n^{-delta} of convergence of the empirical spectral distribution of n^{-1/2} M_n to the circular law under a (2+eps)-th moment assumption, and the exact dependence of delta on eps.
source: Tao and Vu: From the Littlewood-Offord problem to the circular law, survey with open questions
why_important: Rate of convergence to the circular law under weak moments.
where_it_stands: Rates are known under stronger moments.

title: Low-density genealogical limit of branching coalescing walks
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Prove the proposed low-density, time-rescaled lineage limit for transient branching-coalescing walk and the constrained-Ising analogue, after discarding short-lived branching jitter.
statement_caveat: The two explicitly linked microscopic models are grouped; the undefined dynamic-graph research direction is not a second admitted problem. Spatial positions are forgotten but splitting and merging histories remain.
source: Aldous open problems: Low-density coalescing branching random walk
why_important: Genealogies of branching-coalescing walks at low density.
where_it_stands: A proposed limit with a clear construction.

title: Relaxation of linear-polymer coagulation and fragmentation
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Determine the order of the relaxation time for the reversible polymer coagulation-fragmentation chain, especially fragmentation rate beta_n comparable to1/n.
statement_caveat: Clusters merge at rate2/n per pair; each internal link splits at rate beta. Fixed-beta and small-beta regimes are grouped. The source proves bounds between asymptotic1/sqrt(beta^2+4beta) and1/beta.
source: Aldous open problems: Coagulation-fragmentation mixing
why_important: Relaxation time of a coagulation-fragmentation chain.
where_it_stands: A reversible chain with explicit stationary law.

title: Explicit stationary law of the leftmost Hammersley drift-jump particles
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Give a useful explicit joint stationary law for the ordered particles which drift at speed x and jump left at rate1 Poisson space-time points.
statement_caveat: The1993 notes already contain a patience-sorting representation and small-k calculations. The1999 paper Section5.2 uses the stationary process for limit theorems. Those established representations are not counted as newly solved open work.
source: Aldous open problems: One-dimensional drift-jump particle process
why_important: Stationary law of drifting particles with Poisson jumps.
where_it_stands: Hammersley-process tools give stationary measures.

title: Limit of the optimal online random spanning-tree cost
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and combinatorial probability
statement: Prove existence and determine the limiting optimal mean cost of an online spanning tree of the complete randomly weighted graph.
statement_caveat: Combinatorial random-order and Poisson offer models are grouped, but their finite-n costs differ. The draft explicitly lacks a complete asymptotic equivalence proof. Numerical estimates near1.9 are not certified limits.
source: Aldous-Angel-Berestycki: Online random weight minimal spanning trees, draft2008
locator: Conjecture PDFp2;Theorem3 PDFp4; author open page
why_important: Optimal online spanning trees on random weights.
where_it_stands: Bounds of the right order exist.

title: When is the coalescence time twice the meeting time (Kingman behaviour for coalescing walks)?
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, sandpiles and KPZ
statement: Open Problem 2. Assuming (5.2), under what further conditions can one prove E T^coal ~ 2 tau_meet as n -> infinity? (5.3) [Section 5.5, PDF p. 15: 'Return to the setting of Section 5.1 - chains are associated chains run at half speed. Write tau_meet for the mean meeting time from independent uniform starts. In a sequence of chains with n -> infinity, impose a condition such as the following. For each delta > 0, n^{-2} |{(i,j) : E T^meet_{ij} not in (1 +- delta) tau_meet}| -> 0 as n -> infinity. (5.2)' Here T^coal is the time for n coalescing walkers started one per vertex to coalesce to one, T^meet_{ij} the meeting time of two independent copies of the chain started at i and j; the geometry is a weighted graph (nu_{ij}) with the standardisation (2.2) of Section 2 (sum_j nu_{ij} = 1). Same page: 'That such a result is anticipated has been folklore since 1989, when Cox [23] proved (5.3) for the torus [0, m-1]^d in dimension d >= 2.' The source also proposes a two-stage route: Stage 1 (m fixed walkers coalesce in mean ~ 2(1 - 1/m) tau_meet, 'likely ... without further assumptions') and Stage 2 (n walkers reduce to m(n) -> infinity clusters in time o(tau_meet)), and says 'See [42] for a recent extensive study of this problem, and the current best results.']
source: Aldous: Interacting particle systems as stochastic social dynamics (Bernoulli 2013)
why_important: Coalescence time versus meeting time for coalescing walks.
where_it_stands: Proved under mixing conditions in related settings.

title: The boundary case of the collision phase transition on comb graphs
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: The source excludes "the boundary case gamma = 1/3 in our analysis, which we conjecture to fall into the regime of Theorem 4.1-(1)", i.e. the infinite collision property.
why_important: The boundary case of collision for walks on comb graphs.
where_it_stands: The other cases are settled in the source.

title: Monotonicity of the two-point connection probability in the distance on Z^2
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^2 with parameter p. Source: 'on the square lattice is an open question to prove that the probability of the origin being connected to the vertex (0,n) is monotone in n' and, after the construction of a transitive graph without the property, 'it remains an open question whether graphs like Z^d satisfy the monotonic property or not'. Question: for every p in (0,1), is n -> P_p(0 <-> (0,n)) non-increasing on Z^2 (and on Z^d)? [The source traces the question to Hammersley and Welsh (1965) in first-passage percolation.]
source: Campos, de Lima: The probability of connection between two vertices cannot be monotone with the distance for Bernoulli percolation on transitive graphs (2026)
locator: Abstract and Introduction, PDF p. 1; Section 3, PDF p. 4
why_important: Monotonicity of connection probabilities in planar percolation.
where_it_stands: Counterexamples exist in other settings; Z^2 symmetry is the tool.

title: Alon-Peres conjecture: non-backtracking walks of length C sqrt(n) are rarely simple (minimum degree 3)
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Conjecture 1.5 (Alon-Peres). For any eps > 0, there exists a C = C(eps) such that if Gamma is a graph on n vertices with all degrees at least 3, and k > C sqrt(n), then for any edge delta, the probability that a length-k random non-backtracking walk starting with delta is simple is less than eps. [The source proves the fixed-degree (regular) case; 'one could also explore analogs of these statements for (non-backtracking) closed loops'.]
source: Dozier: The birthday paradox for non-backtracking walks on regular graphs (2026)
why_important: Alon-Peres conjecture on non-backtracking walks.
where_it_stands: Proved for walks of larger length.

title: Positivity of the vacant-set threshold u* for random interlacements on the Sierpinski gasket times Z
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: For random interlacements on G x Z with G the discrete Sierpinski gasket graph, is the vacant-set percolation threshold u* strictly positive?
source: Drewitz, Rath, Sapozhnikov: An introduction to random interlacements, preliminary version of the SpringerBriefs book
why_important: Vacant-set percolation for random interlacements on fractal graphs.
where_it_stands: Positivity is known on many transient graphs.

title: Existence of alpha-determinantal processes for 0 <= alpha <= 2
domain_name: Random matrices and free probability
statement: Conjecture 40. If K is a (real) kernel defining a self-adjoint, non-negative integral operator on L^2(Lambda) and 0 <= alpha <= 2, then the alpha-determinantal process with kernel K exists. However, if alpha > 2, then there exists such a kernel K for which there is no corresponding alpha-determinantal process. [The source verifies the second half for alpha > 4 with the 3 x 3 matrix K = ((2,-1,-1),(-1,2,-1),(-1,-1,2)), whose alpha-determinant is 2(4 - alpha)(alpha + 1) < 0 for alpha > 4; an alpha-determinantal process has joint intensities det_alpha(K(x_i, x_j)), where det_alpha A = sum over permutations of alpha^{n - #cycles} prod a_{i sigma(i)}.]
source: Hough, Krishnapur, Peres, Virag: Determinantal processes and independence (Probab. Surveys 2006)
why_important: Existence of alpha-determinantal processes.
where_it_stands: Known for special values of alpha.

title: Problem 20.11 of Janson (2012): a scaling limit object in the condensation regime
domain_name: Branching structures, trees and recursive equations
statement: "Is there some kind of similar limiting object in the case nu < 1 (after suitable scaling)?" - a counterpart of the continuum random tree, or of the stable trees, for subcritical weight sequences.
source: Janson: Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation (Probab. Surveys 2012)
why_important: Scaling limits of simply generated trees in the condensation regime.
where_it_stands: Condensation is described at the level of local limits.

title: Dependence of the expected free minimal spanning forest degree on the Cayley graph
domain_name: Percolation, spanning forests and spatial graphs
statement: Question 6.13. Given a finitely generated group Gamma, does the expected degree of a vertex in the FMSF of a Cayley graph of Gamma depend on which Cayley graph is used? As discussed in the proof of Corollary 3.24, the analogous result is true for the FSF. [FMSF = free minimal spanning forest: edges carry i.i.d. uniform labels and an edge is kept iff its endpoints are not joined by a path of edges with strictly smaller labels; WMSF = wired version, where paths 'through infinity' also count. For the free uniform spanning forest the expected degree is 2 + 2 beta_1^{(2)}(Gamma), a group invariant (Lyons).]
source: Lyons, Peres, Schramm: Minimal spanning forests (Ann. Probab. 2006)
why_important: Does the free minimal spanning forest depend on the Cayley graph?
where_it_stands: Known for related invariants.

title: Mixing on large monotone subsets of the hypercube
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For an increasing subset V of the binary N-cube with at least half its vertices, is lazy induced-subgraph random-walk mixing always O(N*log N)?
statement_caveat: The author page gives an O(N^3) theorem of Ding-Mossel and conjectures N*log N. This is the induced graph walk, whose stationary law is degree weighted, not automatically uniform.
source: Yuval Peres: related open Markov-chain problems
why_important: Mixing on monotone subsets of the hypercube.
where_it_stands: Bounds of polynomial order are known.

title: Dimension-linear relaxation time for generalized reflected Brownian motion
domain_name: Brownian motion, Levy processes and SPDE
statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 1.3, the generalized reflected Brownian motion GRBM(R, mu, Sigma, U) is uniformly exponentially ergodic with exponent of order 1/d: there exist W : R^d -> [1, infinity) and C > 0 such that ||P^t(x, .) - pi(.)||_{TV} <= W(x) exp(-C t / d). This would mean the relaxation time to global equilibrium is of order d for a class of GRBMs.
source: Exponential ergodicity and convergence for generalized reflected Brownian motion
why_important: Relaxation time of reflected Brownian motion in high dimension.
where_it_stands: Exponential ergodicity is proved under the stated assumptions.

title: Catalano-Lavenant conjecture: the diagonal couplings of the uniform law are farthest from independence
domain_name: Optimal transport, statistics and inference
statement: Conjecture 1.1 ([4, Remark 3]). Let lambda denote the uniform probability measure on [0,1]. Then the diagonal and antidiagonal couplings (id,id)_# lambda and (id, 1 - id)_# lambda maximize the 2-Wasserstein distance from the independent coupling lambda (x) lambda among all elements of Pi(lambda, lambda).
